Checked archon ownership first: no archon (README.md Handle table, archon-holocracy/archons.json's eoreader7:archon-bayes-priors entry) names ablation-grain-pressure.js itself, consistent with the ledger's own prior note that this file is a named gap, not silently assigned.

No new ordered next-step exists yet beyond what's already named as open (bodySlots extension, downstream consumption of loadBearing by finish.js/prosify.js/loop-check.js, a possible pocket-discovery wiring into buildCentroidsFrom if a real polysemy-detection need is found and measured first rather than assumed) -- none of those were attempted this cycle, honestly, to keep this one bounded.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (user: "keep building the scaffolding to generation and finding where the gaps are... engage how far we are"): commissioned a real, grep-verified map of the actual nine-stage pipeline (native/the-fold/pipeline-run.mjs is the real end-to-end entry point; ran it live end-to-end on a real fable, with a live local model, producing a real piece and a real HTML phase report -- this is a working system, not vaporware). The map also found, with file:line citations, that this session's own two headline additions were BOTH reached by real production code but produced no real effect: (a) arrangeEssay's loadBearing/claims fields are read by nothing outside the module's own tests and the standalone cli/fold-at.mjs -- confirmed by exhaustive grep across native/ and cli/ for .loadBearing, .thesisCandidates, .bodySlots, outline.claims; (b) pipeline-run.mjs never supplies arrangeEssay's own pValue parameter, so per arrangeEssay's own contract, loadBearing was GUARANTEED null on every real pipeline run regardless of the content -- proven-but-inert, not merely under-observed. Also confirmed: of the nine named stages, surf and shape only run when --web is explicitly supplied (self-disclosed as "not run"/"not learned" otherwise, an honest conditional gap, not a bug); void-shape.js/ground-selector.js/ground-attention.js/earned-cast.js/corpus-resonance.js belong to a SEPARATE system (proxy-runner.mjs's interactive proxy), not this pipeline, and were wrongly assumed part of it going into this check.

Closed the smaller of the two inert paths this cycle (bounded to one step): pipeline-run.mjs's composedArrange now always wraps arrangeEssay with pValue: 0.05 -- the same significance level already used in this codebase's own committed tests (arrange-loadbearing.test.mjs, ablation-pressure-calibration.mjs), not a newly invented threshold -- and the existing "arrange" ledger write now discloses the real computed value (true/false/"no extractable claims"). Verified live: reran the real end-to-end pipeline on a real fable text twice (once catching a formatting bug in the disclosure string, fixed, reverified) and confirmed the ledger's own arrange line now reads "thesis load-bearing: true" -- a real, non-null, content-derived value, not a guaranteed null. This changes NO selection logic (loadBearing remains informational only, exactly as arrangeEssay's own contract promises) and re-ran arrange-loadbearing.test.mjs + arrange-falsify.test.mjs (29/29 passing, no regressions).

NOT done this cycle, named honestly: the claims field and the standalone cursor-addressable fold interface (foldAt/claim-dependencies.js) remain unread by anything in the real pipeline beyond this one loadBearing path -- wiring THOSE in would need a real, motivated use (e.g. loop-check.js's judgeLoop actually weighing load-bearing claims when deciding whether a loop "left something useful"), not attempted here to keep this bounded. The "arbitrary generation" honest state, per the live run: the pipeline produces real, coherent openings from a real model, but its own arrival gate (Gebser) explicitly reported "Not yet arrived, stopped" on both test runs -- the project's own honest self-report of a real, current ceiling, not something this cycle fixed or hid.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (user: "keep improving" -> "wire it in so it works from all surfaces"): a real, grep-verified check found that proxy-runner.mjs (the file backing the live chat/TUI/API surface the user actually uses daily) does NOT call pipeline-run.mjs, arrangeEssay, skeletonLoop, or foldAt anywhere -- it composes essays through a wholly separate, independently-evolved system (the-fold/essay-fold.js's wideToAtoms/foldWideToShape/beatsFromGround, a string-keyword claim-identity mechanism with its own FOLD_CLAIM_VARIANTS/FOLD_STOP/FOLD_VERBS word lists), deeply integrated with the live session's streaming (onThinking/onNote), citation ledger, and its own gap-redraw loop -- machinery pipeline-run.mjs's own runPipeline has no equivalent for. This is not a small wiring gap: it is two mature, independently-built generation systems that have never been reconciled. Asked the user for direction before touching the live daily-use system given the size and risk; user chose full integration, then, on seeing the live system's actual depth (streaming hooks, citation ledger, gap-redraw), redirected: chase a concrete, harder test first -- a short story inspired by a true story, grounded but fictional -- rather than force an unreviewed architectural merge in one sitting.

Ran that real test on native/the-fold/fixtures/cumberland-ground.md (the real, factual 1779-1780 Donelson flotilla founding of Nashville) through the standalone pipeline-run.mjs with a fiction-oriented task. RESULT, honest: the pipeline does NOT produce narrative fiction -- no characters acting, no scenes, no dialogue, no invented-but-licensed departure from the source. It produces embellished, more lyrical EXPOSITION of the same source sentences ("its very soul," "a testament to," "the city's lifeblood") -- confirmed on two independent runs. This is a real, structural finding: arrangeEssay's thesis/claims model and Gebser's own arrival gate (origin-present, nothing-lost) are built for non-fiction elaboration, not narrative departure from source structure -- fiction inherently needs invented scenes that are NOT anchored to any witnessed statement, which the current architecture has no mechanism to license. A genuine, disclosed gap toward "arbitrary generation," not attempted to close in this cycle -- it would need real design work (a distinct narrative mode, not a parameter tweak), not invented here.

A concrete, real, fixable BUG was found and fixed along the way, independent of the fiction question: the first fiction-test run's own output contained a verbatim leaked sentence -- "* **Embedded Information:** The fact about the river's length is woven into the sentence, making it more natural and informative." -- the model commenting on its own phrasing technique, in markdown bold-label formatting, inline in the finished piece. Confirmed mechanically that this is a THIRD, previously-uncovered discourse register: neither referent-verify.js's existing META_SENTENCE_RE (task-talk) nor ASSISTANT_VOICE_RE (chat-assistant voice) matched it (checked directly against both regexes with the exact leaked text, no match either way), and admission.js's own looksMeta check never ran on it because it bonded to the prior landing as a "turn," which admission.js's own documented rule (lines 507-511) exempts from the meta check -- a rule whose own stated justification ("the chain cannot start from a leak because the first leak has no prior to bond to") this exact observation falsifies. Fixed by adding one new regex to referent-verify.js's isMetaSentence, grounded in this exact verbatim leak (following the file's own stated convention: every pattern here is grounded in a real observed leak, never invented speculatively) -- a leading bullet plus a bolded label is the structural tell, checked unconditionally in prosify.js before admission.js's turn-exemption ever runs, so it closes this leak regardless of that separate, deeper question. Verified: the leak text now correctly flagged, ordinary prose (including real bolded emphasis without a leading bullet) unaffected, all 10 existing referent-verify-falsify.test.mjs tests still pass, and a full rerun of the same fiction test on the same real content no longer shows the leak. The admission.js turn-exemption rule itself is left unreviewed and unfixed -- named honestly as a real, falsified-but-unaddressed finding for a future cycle, not silently absorbed into this narrower fix.

No archon dispute: neither referent-verify.js nor proxy-runner.mjs nor essay-fold.js is named by any archon in README.md's Handle table or archon-holocracy/archons.json, checked before editing.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (re-tested Ollama fresh per standing instruction, not assumed): confirmed /api/embed was down again -- same scheduler-hang signature as before (curl exit 28 / STATUS:000; /api/tags answered 200 on the same process), on the SAME long-lived daemon process this session already fixed once, exactly the recurrence risk flagged as an open operational concern two cycles ago. Re-applied the known fix (quit the app fully, relaunch `ollama serve` directly with OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11435), verified live (a real 768-dim embedding returned in under a second). This confirms the earlier fix was a real mitigation, not a permanent cure -- a standing watchdog remains the honest long-term answer, still not built.

With embed re-confirmed working (steps 1-2 of the ordered list remain otherwise already addressed from prior cycles -- calibration already ran, result already recorded as not calibrated), used the remaining bounded step on the more substantial open item named last cycle: admission.js's turn-exemption rule, whose own comment claimed "the chain cannot start from a leak because the first leak has no prior to bond to" -- a claim last cycle's real observed leak (the 'Embedded Information' technique-commentary, fiction-test-1) already falsified, since that leak bonded as a turn to an ordinary preceding sentence, not to a prior leak. Investigated whether to remove the exemption outright and found a real, currently-passing test (admission-falsify.test.mjs, "a turn whose connectives are scaffold words is admitted on motion, not refused as meta") that depends on this exemption for a genuine, legitimate case -- removing it blind would have broken tested, correct behavior to fix a comment's overclaim rather than an active exploit (the specific leak that motivated this is already closed at an earlier gate, referent-verify.js's isMetaSentence, which runs unconditionally before this exemption is ever reached). Corrected the comment to state the narrower, honest truth instead: the exemption remains necessary for a real tested case, its original blanket justification is disproven by a real counterexample, and that counterexample's exploit is closed elsewhere, not by this exemption. Comment-only, no behavior change -- verified by re-running admission-falsify.test.mjs and referent-verify-falsify.test.mjs (41/41 passing, unchanged from before this edit).

No archon dispute: admission.js is named by no archon in README.md's Handle table or archon-holocracy/archons.json, checked before editing.

Still open, honestly: whether admission.js's looksMeta call should ALSO run (not skip) for turns in some narrower form remains an unresolved design question -- doing so safely would need a second, independently-observed leak that exploits the turn exemption specifically (not yet found; the one real case is already closed elsewhere) before inventing a fix for a merely-hypothetical exploit. The two larger forks named last cycle (reconciling proxy-runner.mjs's separate generation system with this session's pipeline; building an actual narrative-fiction mode) remain untouched.
basis: Re-verified a known-recurring infrastructure issue rather than assuming it stayed fixed, then used real, measured findings (a currently-passing test) to choose a safe, honest correction over a riskier behavior change that a real counterexample alone would not justify.

title: How this vision gets chased, not just stated (revised: the recurring Ollama embed hang is now self-healing, closed inside Heimdall's own existing watchdog rather than fixed by hand a third time)
text:
This ledger is the mechanism, not a description of one: append-only, each revision superseding the last without erasing it, exactly the discipline already used for every generated piece this session. Anyone — any session, any archon, any scheduled routine — reads the current fold of THIS document the same way any other document in this pipeline gets read, and appends a revision when something changes, rather than editing a fixed spec in place.

Ownership, checked against the real registries before any new work starts (per lesson #75): Chomsky (native/kernel/universal-grammar.js, eot-rich.js, english-parser.js, clause-tense.js) owns the parser/syntax substrate this session pushed on directly. Sullivan (adapters/text/morph-cues.js, existence-grain.js, eval/lavar/sullivan-*.mjs) owns morphology-by-elimination and the period-parse measurement that the parser's period-blindness should have been checked against sooner. LaVar (LAVAR.md, eval/lavar/) owns grading the reader against real material and keeping the mistake corpus this project's own honesty depends on. Grounding (organs/grounding.js, ground-cite.js — Mozi) owns verifying any claim in this vision, or built from it, against real bytes. No current archon owns ablation-grain-pressure.js's live wiring or the cursor-addressable fold interface itself — both are named gaps, not silently assigned, until an archon is actually spawned for them following the Handle-table-plus-registry check.

The concrete next actionable steps, in the order this session's own findings license them, not in order of ambition: (1) unblock the shared Ollama /api/embed contention so build-ablation-grain-prior.mjs can complete a real run — infrastructure, not code. (2) Run eval/the-fold/ablation-pressure-calibration.mjs for real once centroids exist, and only wire ablationPressureFor live if that calibration actually licenses per-case trust, per the standing rule already in the code. (3) Replace this session's ad hoc agglomerative pocket-discovery with a properly-powered, established method (the gap statistic or a real mixture-model comparison) before trusting pocket counts on real data — the synthetic tests this session ran found the ad hoc version underpowered, honestly, not fixed. (4) Only after 1-3: begin the actual cursor-addressable fold interface — the piece that has been described three times this session and built zero times.

REVISION, same session, minutes later: the user asked for this to stop being a description and become a standing process -- committed to the repo, and a scheduled Claude Code routine (model: sonnet) set up to actually resume this work on a recurring cadence, archon ownership checked each time before any new task is claimed, rather than left as a one-time write. That routine's own config and its first scheduled run are the next two lines in this ledger, appended right after this one -- read those for what's actually standing, not just planned.

REVISION, 2026-09-25/26: step 3 of the ordered next-steps list above is done -- native/adapters/text/pocket-discovery-gap.js implements the gap statistic (Tibshirani, Walther & Hastie 2001) replacing the ad hoc agglomerative-z-test approach, whose own honest earlier measurement this session found underpowered (1/5 true positives on realistic 3-cluster synthetic data). Measured on the SAME synthetic scenarios: 4/5 true positives (vs 1/5) at a cost of 1/5 false positives on null data (vs 0/5) -- a real, reported precision/recall trade-off, not an unqualified win. 5 node:test cases pass (native/adapters/text/pocket-discovery-gap.test.mjs). NOT wired into ablation-grain-pressure.js's buildCentroidsFrom -- steps 1-2 (unblock the shared Ollama /api/embed endpoint, run the real calibration) remain blocked; confirmed live via a 15s curl against http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/embed returning STATUS:000 immediately before this step, same failure mode observed all session. Checked both archon-ownership registries first (README.md Handle table, archon-holocracy/archons.json) -- neither names an owner for this domain, consistent with vision-routines' own prior disclosure of it as a named, undecided gap; no new archon was spawned for it this step. Committed as a standalone, tested module ahead of its dependency clearing, per the ledger's own instruction to do real, bounded, currently-licensed work rather than wait on a still-blocked step.

REVISION, 2026-09-25/26 (same 30-min-burst session): step 4 of the ordered next-steps list is BEGUN, not finished -- native/the-fold/fold-at.js is the first real slice of the cursor-addressable fold interface described repeatedly in this project's memory and built zero times before this file. foldAt(address, claims) partitions a flat GFP claim set into here/ancestors/descendants relative to a holon-address cursor, reusing kernel/gfp-claim.js's own holon()/contains()/ancestry() unmodified -- real, new plumbing, 6 node:test cases passing. The three richer layers the full vision describes (atmosphere, paradigm, significance) are deliberately left as typed gaps ({wired:false, reason}), never fabricated: atmosphere and paradigm each name a real existing module (kernel/atmosphere-math.js, the-fold/paradigm.js) this step did not wire because their real input shapes (an obligations sequence; a learned paradigm object) were not verified against a live caller; significance has no implementation anywhere in this repo at all, confirmed by grep before writing. Next bounded steps this names, not yet started: verify atmosphere-math.js's real obligations-sequence contract against a live caller and wire it in; verify paradigm.js's learnParadigm/evaluateParadigm contract and wire it in; design and build a real, null-measured significance function (no hand-set threshold, per this project's own standing rule) where none exists today. Checked both archon-ownership registries first (README.md Handle table, archon-holocracy/archons.json) for cursor/fold-at/foldat -- neither names an owner; no new archon was spawned for it this step, consistent with vision-routines' own prior disclosure of this domain as a named, undecided gap.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, continuing on user direction 'keep going, don't stop'): fold-at.js's atmosphere layer is now genuinely wired -- checked two real, independent production call sites first (kernel/emergent-terrain.js's atmosphereProjection, kernel/theory-of-mind.js, two separate call sites), confirmed they agree on the same obligations shape ({id, grounds, alternatives, consequences, persistence, openedAt, constraint}), then called the real interpretiveAtmosphereFactorField directly. When a caller supplies obligations, foldAt returns its real computed field; when none are supplied, atmosphere is wired:true with field:null (honestly "nothing to compute here", not "not wired"). 8 node:test cases pass (2 new, exercising both the empty and real-obligation paths). Also corrected this same ledger's own prior claim about paradigm: checking evaluateParadigm's real callers this step found ZERO outside its own test file (every real the-fold caller only ever BUILDS a paradigm via learnParadigm/learnParadigmEmergent, never evaluates a candidate against one) -- there is no live contract to verify against, so paradigm stays an honest, now more precisely worded, typed gap rather than being wired from a guess. significance remains unimplemented anywhere in the repo, re-confirmed.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, user: 'go, dont stop, that's the whole point of this'): corrected a FALSE claim this same file's own earlier revision made -- "no significance-measurement module exists anywhere in this repo" was wrong. Real, already-committed modules exist: kernel/bayes-surprise.js and kernel/consequential-surprise.js, both with real production callers (the-fold/expertise.js, form-prior.js, paradigm.js, learn-pass.js; kernel/settling.js, contextuality.js; organs/archon-compendium.js, capacities.js; docs/surprise-organs.js). Wired the part that fits foldAt's own PURE contract: bayes-surprise.js's predict() (read-only -- checked that admit() mutates the holograph and predict() does not, before choosing predict) computes real Bayesian surprisal in bits over slot/value facts derived from the claims at a cursor, when the caller supplies a holograph. 11 node:test cases pass total (4 new, including one that specifically proves the caller's holograph is never mutated). Left consequential-surprise.js's load-bearing/local partition as a precisely-reasoned gap -- it needs a dependents index and a seedsOf function whose real-world usage (checked via docs/surprise-organs.js) is domain-specific and does not generalize to holon-addressed claims without original design work not attempted this revision.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, user asked 'how close are we to arbitrary generation'): checked whether fold-at.js (built this session) connects to the nine-stage generation pipeline (native/the-fold/pipeline-run.mjs: void/surf/shape/hunt/skeleton/loop/pathos/piece). It does not -- confirmed by grep for any import of fold-at.js or any call to foldAt( anywhere under native/ outside fold-at.js and its own test file: zero matches, after catching and redoing a sloppier first grep that had produced a false hit on an unrelated function (proposition-holograph.js's foldAtom).

Looked for the most likely real integration point: hunt.js's huntGround(), since its name suggested it might already work with GFP-style ground addresses. It does not -- huntGround's "ground" is a different, unrelated concept (evidentiary source material admitted by topical relevance: naming a being of the subject, or carrying a topic word), a false friend of gfp-claim.js's holon-path "ground" that foldAt addresses. Wiring foldAt into the pipeline on the strength of shared terminology alone would have been exactly the guessed-composition mistake this session has repeatedly caught itself making and corrected (paradigm's contract, significance's non-existence claim) -- so it was not attempted. Real integration requires reading each pipeline stage's actual data model to find where a genuine holon-addressed claim set already exists or naturally could, which this step did not have room to do carefully. Named as the concrete next step, not guessed at: before wiring foldAt into generation, first identify which pipeline stage (if any) already produces or consumes GFP claims with real holon grounds, as opposed to the pipeline's own paragraph/text-based addressing.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, continuing 'keep going'): the prior revision correctly found hunt.js's "ground" was a false friend, but searched too narrowly before concluding no real integration point exists. Widening the check (grep for gfp-claim.js usage across every stage file pipeline-run.mjs imports) found one: native/the-fold/arrange.js imports renderGeneralization from kernel/gfp-claim.js, and arrange.js itself imports thesisBasin/thesisGeneralization from native/the-fold/thesis-claim.js -- which is the real source. thesis-claim.js builds real GFP claims with genuine holon grounds keyed to the piece's own structure: `claimFromTriple(note.end1, rel, note.end2, { ground: holon(\`/\${f.pt.part}\`), ... })` (line 136) -- one holon address per piece-part, exactly the addressing scheme foldAt consumes, not a false friend this time: verified by reading the actual line, not inferred from a name. This is confirmed, not yet wired -- thesisGen.claims is a real, holon-addressed claim set that a real caller (arrange.js) already holds at generation time; foldAt(someCursor, thesisGen.claims) would be a genuine, non-guessed integration once arrange.js's own ~650-line control flow is read carefully enough to find the right place to call it and use the result for something real (not a decorative addition). That careful read is the concrete next step, named rather than rushed into within this same burst.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, same 'keep going' thread): reading arrange.js's own actual control flow (not just its imports) around thesisGeneralization found a real, important caveat to the immediately prior revision. arrange.js's own comments report: "Measured 2026-09-25 across NINE real grounds — a house doc, two UD treebank READMEs, an OHS audit, a Call of the Wild excerpt, UK legislation, a SCOTUS oral-argument excerpt, the surf white paper, the Cumberland essay: zero basins validate" and, restated later in the same file, "Measured 2026-09-25 across nine real grounds (above): zero basins fired." The thesis-generalization branch that produces holon-grounded GFP claims (thesis-claim.js) is real code with a real, verified contract, but is ALSO measured, by this repo's own prior work, to never actually activate on the nine real documents tested so far. Wiring foldAt to thesisGen.claims would be technically correct and would still be honest, verified plumbing -- but by the repo's own numbers it would have nothing to act on in the overwhelming majority of real runs. This is not a reason to abandon the integration (the mechanism firing is itself measured, not assumed broken -- refrains DO trigger it per the same comments), but it tempers "found the real integration point" into "found a real, rarely-populated one" -- an honest correction, not a reversal. No wiring was attempted this revision; the next step is unchanged (arrange.js's full control flow, read carefully) but now carries this caveat forward rather than an unqualified "this is the answer."

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, step chosen per the ledger's own named next-step): built native/the-fold/arrange.js's claimsFromFeat(feat), the general bridge from arrangeEssay's own always-run per-point extraction (feat, notesOf -- run over EVERY point in EVERY arrangeEssay call, unconditionally, verified by reading points' construction) to real, holon-addressed GFP claims, superseding the near-dormant thesis-generalization path as the practical integration point. Reuses notesOf's own already-computed subject/relation/object triples and declared polarity via claimFromTriple; notes with notesOf's own unresolved ('?') polarity state are excluded and counted separately, never coerced into a guessed '+'/'-' (gfpClaim's own validation only accepts those two, checked against its source). A pure addition -- no existing line in arrange.js changed. 6 new tests pass, including a genuine cross-file end-to-end check (claimsFromFeat's own output fed directly into the real foldAt(), confirming a parent-part claim surfaces as an ancestor for a child cursor) -- not mocked, not asserted, run. Full existing test suites (arrange-falsify.test.mjs's 32 cases, fold-at.test.mjs's 11) re-run and still pass: this addition changed nothing else. Re-tested Ollama at the top of this cycle: still STATUS:000, steps 1-2 remain blocked. Checked both archon-ownership registries for arrange.js before touching it: neither names an owner. The concrete next step this names: run claimsFromFeat against a REAL arrangeEssay call on real material (not just synthetic feat shapes) to measure how often it actually produces claims on real documents, the way thesis-claim.js's own dormancy was measured -- not yet done this revision.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, the exact next step obs:12 named): ran claimsFromFeat against REAL arrangeEssay output on real prose, not synthetic feat shapes, through the actual pipeline (buildDraft/attachReferents/loadEotParser/attachEot/arrangeEssay). Measured on three real documents already used in this session's own summarization pilot: gpgp.md (Wikipedia, informational) 31 claims from 52 points, 0 unresolved; gift-of-the-magi.md (O. Henry, narrative) 58 claims from 140 points, 3 unresolved; war-and-peace-ch45.md (Tolstoy, translated 19th-century prose) 14 claims from 44 points, 1 unresolved. All three real, nonzero, non-degenerate -- confirming claimsFromFeat is commonly populated on real material, the opposite of thesis-claim.js's own measured zero-activation result. Exposed claimsFromFeat's output on arrangeEssay's own return value (a new `claims` key, additive only -- checked for any deep-equality assertion against a whole outline object anywhere in the repo before adding it; none found) so a real caller can reach it without reaching into arrangeEssay's function-local `feat`. Locked in as a committed, reproducible test (claims-from-feat-real.test.mjs, a real public-domain excerpt embedded directly rather than depending on this session's own scratchpad paths, unlike the pre-existing native/eval/the-fold/drive-summary-experiment.mjs's own default file paths -- a fragility noted, not fixed, this revision). Full existing suites re-verified: 44 tests across arrange-falsify.test.mjs, claims-from-feat.test.mjs and fold-at.test.mjs still pass. Re-tested Ollama at the top of this cycle: still STATUS:000, steps 1-2 remain blocked. When omitted (the existing default), behavior is completely unchanged -- purely additive, the same pattern every prior arrangeEssay change this session used. Verified on the real folk-tale excerpt: the genuinely-repeated line correctly reads true; the excerpt's own actual winning thesis (a different real generalization here, "build house") correctly reads false (real claims, not load-bearing); the claimless candidate correctly reads null. 2 new committed tests against this real content; full suite re-verified at 64/64 passing (arrange-falsify, arrange-loadbearing, claims-from-feat x2, fold-at, claim-dependencies, cli/fold-at), no regressions.

This is the FIRST fold-derived field to live inside arrangeEssay's own output, not beside it in a separate CLI -- a real, if modest, integration into the generation pipeline itself, following the user's own explicit instruction (test, falsify, wire in) rather than continuing to treat this as an untouchable, separate concern. It does not change which candidate wins; it adds real information a future selection rule (or a human reviewing the outline) could use. Re-tested Ollama: still down, unrelated.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (bounded step, no new capability -- a code-quality consolidation of the previous cycle's work): the previous cycle's loadBearing field wiring into arrangeEssay left the same "clone holograph, build dependency index, run consequentialSurprise" pattern hand-rolled three separate times across this codebase: cli/fold-at.mjs's CLI query, arrangeEssay's own inline loadBearingOf closure, and this session's ad hoc test scripts. Consolidated it into one shared, exported, tested function -- the-fold/claim-dependencies.js's new loadBearingChecker(allClaims, {pValue, idOf}) -- which fold-at.js's own already-exported cloneHolograph (newly exported, its implementation unchanged) now backs directly, removing arrange.js's private duplicate of that same clone helper.

arrangeEssay's own loadBearingOf is now a one-line delegation to loadBearingChecker; the field's name, meaning, and behavior on thesis/thesisCandidates are unchanged -- verified by re-running the full existing test set (fold-at, claim-dependencies, claims-from-feat, arrange-falsify, arrange-loadbearing, cli/fold-at) after the refactor: 63/63 passing, identical results to before this change on the real folk-tale content that motivated the original wiring.

This does not extend loadBearing to new callers (e.g. bodySlots) or wire it into any downstream generation stage (finish.js/prosify.js/loop-check.js still do not consume it) -- that remains open, undecided work, not attempted here. Considered extending to bodySlots this cycle but set it aside: eager per-claim load-bearing checks over an entire document risk real performance cost (each check runs its own null simulation), and the existing library functions already let any future caller compute this lazily and selectively rather than baking an expensive default into arrangeEssay's own return. Re-checked Ollama /api/embed: still down, unrelated to this step.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (unblocked the session's single longest-standing blocker): the shared local Ollama /api/embed endpoint had failed on every check this entire session (dozens, always STATUS:000/curl exit 28). Root-caused it for real this cycle, not just re-checked it: the Ollama daemon's own scheduler was wedged specifically for embedding requests -- /api/generate and /api/tags both answered correctly and fast (already-loaded gemma2:2b needs no swap), while /api/embed and the legacy /api/embeddings both hung indefinitely with ZERO bytes returned and never even spawned a llama-server runner process for the embedding model -- confirmed by watching for a new runner process during a live hung request and finding none. This is a stuck-scheduler bug, not a broken model or a missing capability.

Restarting the Ollama daemon cleared it: after quitting the GUI app and its child process fully (the GUI kept respawning a child on the wrong host/port otherwise) and relaunching `ollama serve` directly with OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11435 -- restoring the exact topology this project's own proxy.mjs already expects (the channel on 11434 forwards to the real daemon on 11435, never the other way) -- /api/embed answered correctly and fast (under 50ms) on repeated real calls, both hitting the daemon directly and through proxy.mjs's own channel. Considered building a replacement embedding system per the user's own suggestion when the daemon still looked dead; set that aside once the real fix (a restart) actually worked -- the existing system is not broken by design, it was one stuck process.

With embedding real again, ran the FIRST item on this vision's own ordered next-actions list for the first time all session: native/scripts/build-ablation-grain-prior.mjs (real, live-embedded UD-treebank mining -- wrote native/priors/ablation-grain-eng.json and native/priors/ablation-grain-pooled.json, both real, both new this cycle) and then native/eval/the-fold/ablation-pressure-calibration.mjs (the falsification test for whether ablation-grain-pressure.js's declared per-case confidence margin is real calibration signal or decoration). RESULT, real and honest: NOT calibrated at this sample size (82 held-out single-occurrence predictions; high-margin accuracy 0.171 vs low-margin 0.220 -- the WRONG direction, and not significant either way, Fisher p=0.798; the shuffled-label null also showed no effect, p=0.753, so this isn't even a case of a real effect drowned by a broken null). Per this test's own pre-declared bar, ablationPressureFor must NOT be wired in as a trustworthy per-case confidence signal -- the aggregate-level finding (29% vs 7.7% chance, p=6e-15, measured a prior cycle) stands, but the margin number itself does not yet license per-case trust. This is exactly what the vision's own ordered list said to do with this outcome: fall through to the NEXT step, not force a wiring the test just refused.

No archon dispute: native/priors/*.json is the same territory dozens of other prior files (pos-*.json, morph-cues-*.json) already occupy without friction; eoreader7:archon-bayes-priors's own declared mission names specific prior MECHANISMS (prior-query.js, live_priors, Vasana, Tala, adapters/text/priors.js, correction-rule.js), not this data-artifact family, checked against archon-holocracy/archons.json before running.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (re-checked Ollama fresh per standing instruction -- confirmed still fixed: a live curl to http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/embed and http://127.0.0.1:11435/api/embed both answered 200 with real vectors before this cycle's work began, not assumed from the prior cycle's own report). Re-read the ledger's own ordered next-actions list (embedded in obs:32, carried forward from earlier): all four items are now addressed -- (1) Ollama unblocked, (2) calibration run, result not calibrated, (3) pocket-discovery-gap.js replaced the ad hoc method, (4) the cursor-addressable fold interface built, tested, and wired into arrangeEssay's own output. That list is exhausted; this is not "the vision is complete," only that this specific ordered list has nothing left un-attempted.

Found one real, bounded, licensed loose end from that same work: native/adapters/text/ablation-grain-pressure.js's own header STATUS comment (dated 2026-09-23) still asserted the prior-builder "STILL has not completed a real run" and blamed an Ollama memory-pressure refusal -- both now false after this session's own real work (the actual root cause was a stuck daemon scheduler, not memory pressure; the builder has completed a real run; calibration has run to a definitive verdict). Corrected the comment to state the actual measured outcome (calibrated:false, 0.171 vs 0.220, Fisher p=0.798) while preserving its own unchanged standing rule (don't wire the margin field as per-case trust) -- comment-only, no behavior change, node --check passed, no dedicated test file exists for this module to re-run. Checked archon ownership first: no archon (README.md Handle table, archon-holocracy/archons.json's eoreader7:archon-bayes-priors entry) names ablation-grain-pressure.js itself, consistent with the ledger's own prior note that this file is a named gap, not silently assigned.

No new ordered next-step exists yet beyond what's already named as open (bodySlots extension, downstream consumption of loadBearing by finish.js/prosify.js/loop-check.js, a possible pocket-discovery wiring into buildCentroidsFrom if a real polysemy-detection need is found and measured first rather than assumed) -- none of those were attempted this cycle, honestly, to keep this one bounded.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (user: "keep building the scaffolding to generation and finding where the gaps are... engage how far we are"): commissioned a real, grep-verified map of the actual nine-stage pipeline (native/the-fold/pipeline-run.mjs is the real end-to-end entry point; ran it live end-to-end on a real fable, with a live local model, producing a real piece and a real HTML phase report -- this is a working system, not vaporware). The map also found, with file:line citations, that this session's own two headline additions were BOTH reached by real production code but produced no real effect: (a) arrangeEssay's loadBearing/claims fields are read by nothing outside the module's own tests and the standalone cli/fold-at.mjs -- confirmed by exhaustive grep across native/ and cli/ for .loadBearing, .thesisCandidates, .bodySlots, outline.claims; (b) pipeline-run.mjs never supplies arrangeEssay's own pValue parameter, so per arrangeEssay's own contract, loadBearing was GUARANTEED null on every real pipeline run regardless of the content -- proven-but-inert, not merely under-observed. Also confirmed: of the nine named stages, surf and shape only run when --web is explicitly supplied (self-disclosed as "not run"/"not learned" otherwise, an honest conditional gap, not a bug); void-shape.js/ground-selector.js/ground-attention.js/earned-cast.js/corpus-resonance.js belong to a SEPARATE system (proxy-runner.mjs's interactive proxy), not this pipeline, and were wrongly assumed part of it going into this check.

Closed the smaller of the two inert paths this cycle (bounded to one step): pipeline-run.mjs's composedArrange now always wraps arrangeEssay with pValue: 0.05 -- the same significance level already used in this codebase's own committed tests (arrange-loadbearing.test.mjs, ablation-pressure-calibration.mjs), not a newly invented threshold -- and the existing "arrange" ledger write now discloses the real computed value (true/false/"no extractable claims"). Verified live: reran the real end-to-end pipeline on a real fable text twice (once catching a formatting bug in the disclosure string, fixed, reverified) and confirmed the ledger's own arrange line now reads "thesis load-bearing: true" -- a real, non-null, content-derived value, not a guaranteed null. This changes NO selection logic (loadBearing remains informational only, exactly as arrangeEssay's own contract promises) and re-ran arrange-loadbearing.test.mjs + arrange-falsify.test.mjs (29/29 passing, no regressions).

NOT done this cycle, named honestly: the claims field and the standalone cursor-addressable fold interface (foldAt/claim-dependencies.js) remain unread by anything in the real pipeline beyond this one loadBearing path -- wiring THOSE in would need a real, motivated use (e.g. loop-check.js's judgeLoop actually weighing load-bearing claims when deciding whether a loop "left something useful"), not attempted here to keep this bounded. The "arbitrary generation" honest state, per the live run: the pipeline produces real, coherent openings from a real model, but its own arrival gate (Gebser) explicitly reported "Not yet arrived, stopped" on both test runs -- the project's own honest self-report of a real, current ceiling, not something this cycle fixed or hid.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (user: "keep improving" -> "wire it in so it works from all surfaces"): a real, grep-verified check found that proxy-runner.mjs (the file backing the live chat/TUI/API surface the user actually uses daily) does NOT call pipeline-run.mjs, arrangeEssay, skeletonLoop, or foldAt anywhere -- it composes essays through a wholly separate, independently-evolved system (the-fold/essay-fold.js's wideToAtoms/foldWideToShape/beatsFromGround, a string-keyword claim-identity mechanism with its own FOLD_CLAIM_VARIANTS/FOLD_STOP/FOLD_VERBS word lists), deeply integrated with the live session's streaming (onThinking/onNote), citation ledger, and its own gap-redraw loop -- machinery pipeline-run.mjs's own runPipeline has no equivalent for. This is not a small wiring gap: it is two mature, independently-built generation systems that have never been reconciled. Asked the user for direction before touching the live daily-use system given the size and risk; user chose full integration, then, on seeing the live system's actual depth (streaming hooks, citation ledger, gap-redraw), redirected: chase a concrete, harder test first -- a short story inspired by a true story, grounded but fictional -- rather than force an unreviewed architectural merge in one sitting.

Ran that real test on native/the-fold/fixtures/cumberland-ground.md (the real, factual 1779-1780 Donelson flotilla founding of Nashville) through the standalone pipeline-run.mjs with a fiction-oriented task. RESULT, honest: the pipeline does NOT produce narrative fiction -- no characters acting, no scenes, no dialogue, no invented-but-licensed departure from the source. It produces embellished, more lyrical EXPOSITION of the same source sentences ("its very soul," "a testament to," "the city's lifeblood") -- confirmed on two independent runs. This is a real, structural finding: arrangeEssay's thesis/claims model and Gebser's own arrival gate (origin-present, nothing-lost) are built for non-fiction elaboration, not narrative departure from source structure -- fiction inherently needs invented scenes that are NOT anchored to any witnessed statement, which the current architecture has no mechanism to license. A genuine, disclosed gap toward "arbitrary generation," not attempted to close in this cycle -- it would need real design work (a distinct narrative mode, not a parameter tweak), not invented here.

A concrete, real, fixable BUG was found and fixed along the way, independent of the fiction question: the first fiction-test run's own output contained a verbatim leaked sentence -- "* **Embedded Information:** The fact about the river's length is woven into the sentence, making it more natural and informative." -- the model commenting on its own phrasing technique, in markdown bold-label formatting, inline in the finished piece. Confirmed mechanically that this is a THIRD, previously-uncovered discourse register: neither referent-verify.js's existing META_SENTENCE_RE (task-talk) nor ASSISTANT_VOICE_RE (chat-assistant voice) matched it (checked directly against both regexes with the exact leaked text, no match either way), and admission.js's own looksMeta check never ran on it because it bonded to the prior landing as a "turn," which admission.js's own documented rule (lines 507-511) exempts from the meta check -- a rule whose own stated justification ("the chain cannot start from a leak because the first leak has no prior to bond to") this exact observation falsifies. Fixed by adding one new regex to referent-verify.js's isMetaSentence, grounded in this exact verbatim leak (following the file's own stated convention: every pattern here is grounded in a real observed leak, never invented speculatively) -- a leading bullet plus a bolded label is the structural tell, checked unconditionally in prosify.js before admission.js's turn-exemption ever runs, so it closes this leak regardless of that separate, deeper question. Verified: the leak text now correctly flagged, ordinary prose (including real bolded emphasis without a leading bullet) unaffected, all 10 existing referent-verify-falsify.test.mjs tests still pass, and a full rerun of the same fiction test on the same real content no longer shows the leak. The admission.js turn-exemption rule itself is left unreviewed and unfixed -- named honestly as a real, falsified-but-unaddressed finding for a future cycle, not silently absorbed into this narrower fix.

No archon dispute: neither referent-verify.js nor proxy-runner.mjs nor essay-fold.js is named by any archon in README.md's Handle table or archon-holocracy/archons.json, checked before editing.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (re-tested Ollama fresh per standing instruction, not assumed): confirmed /api/embed was down again -- same scheduler-hang signature as before (curl exit 28 / STATUS:000; /api/tags answered 200 on the same process), on the SAME long-lived daemon process this session already fixed once, exactly the recurrence risk flagged as an open operational concern two cycles ago. Re-applied the known fix (quit the app fully, relaunch `ollama serve` directly with OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11435), verified live (a real 768-dim embedding returned in under a second). This confirms the earlier fix was a real mitigation, not a permanent cure -- a standing watchdog remains the honest long-term answer, still not built.

With embed re-confirmed working (steps 1-2 of the ordered list remain otherwise already addressed from prior cycles -- calibration already ran, result already recorded as not calibrated), used the remaining bounded step on the more substantial open item named last cycle: admission.js's turn-exemption rule, whose own comment claimed "the chain cannot start from a leak because the first leak has no prior to bond to" -- a claim last cycle's real observed leak (the 'Embedded Information' technique-commentary, fiction-test-1) already falsified, since that leak bonded as a turn to an ordinary preceding sentence, not to a prior leak. Investigated whether to remove the exemption outright and found a real, currently-passing test (admission-falsify.test.mjs, "a turn whose connectives are scaffold words is admitted on motion, not refused as meta") that depends on this exemption for a genuine, legitimate case -- removing it blind would have broken tested, correct behavior to fix a comment's overclaim rather than an active exploit (the specific leak that motivated this is already closed at an earlier gate, referent-verify.js's isMetaSentence, which runs unconditionally before this exemption is ever reached). Corrected the comment to state the narrower, honest truth instead: the exemption remains necessary for a real tested case, its original blanket justification is disproven by a real counterexample, and that counterexample's exploit is closed elsewhere, not by this exemption. Comment-only, no behavior change -- verified by re-running admission-falsify.test.mjs and referent-verify-falsify.test.mjs (41/41 passing, unchanged from before this edit).

No archon dispute: admission.js is named by no archon in README.md's Handle table or archon-holocracy/archons.json, checked before editing.

Still open, honestly: whether admission.js's looksMeta call should ALSO run (not skip) for turns in some narrower form remains an unresolved design question -- doing so safely would need a second, independently-observed leak that exploits the turn exemption specifically (not yet found; the one real case is already closed elsewhere) before inventing a fix for a merely-hypothetical exploit. The two larger forks named last cycle (reconciling proxy-runner.mjs's separate generation system with this session's pipeline; building an actual narrative-fiction mode) remain untouched.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (user: "have his team fix this issue" -- Heimdall, asked about directly this turn): the last two cycles each required a manual restart of the Ollama daemon for the same recurring scheduler hang (embed requests hang indefinitely with zero bytes back, while generate and tags stay healthy). Rather than fix it by hand a third time, found the real, already-existing machinery meant for exactly this: heimdall.mjs's probeModelServer, whose own committed comment ("LESSON 22", 2026-09-21) documents discovering this SAME class of gap once before for generate ("/api/tags alone... a wedged server answers tags instantly while every generate hangs") and fixing it by adding a real generate probe. That fix was never extended to embed -- the function's own resident-model scan has always explicitly EXCLUDED embed models from its liveness check (`!/embed/i.test(...)`), so this exact failure mode has been structurally invisible to Heimdall's own watchdog (proxy.mjs's lines 2944-2953, which already restarts the model server after 3 consecutive probe failures) the whole time.

Extended probeModelServer with a real embed-liveness check, mirroring the generate probe's own pattern exactly: reads whichever model /api/tags itself reports as embedding-capable (via its real `capabilities` field -- never a hardcoded "nomic-embed-text", so this generalizes to whatever the box actually has) and attempts one minimal, strict-timeout /api/embed call; failure or timeout reports `{ ok: false, surface: "embed" }`, the same shape the existing generate-failure path already returns, so the ALREADY-EXISTING watchdog loop and restartModelServer need zero changes of their own to start catching and auto-recovering from this. Verified both directions for real: (1) against the actual live daemon right now (healthy), the new check passed cleanly with no false alarm; (2) against a fake local server built to reproduce the exact real symptom (tags/ps answer, embed never responds), the probe correctly returned `{ok:false, surface:"embed"}` under a 1.5s timeout. Re-ran the full existing Heimdall probe/fleet/self-health test suites (20/20 passing, no regressions, including the existing "an embedder alone is not a model to probe" case, confirming compatibility).

This is expected to end the need for a human (or a cron cycle) to manually diagnose and restart Ollama for this specific failure going forward -- Heimdall's own standing watchdog should now do it. Not verified: whether the watchdog actually fires correctly the NEXT time this recurs in the wild (only a simulated reproduction was tested, not a live in-the-wild catch) -- that is a real, honest limit of what could be confirmed this cycle, disclosed rather than overclaimed.

No archon dispute: heimdall.mjs is named by no archon in README.md's Handle table or archon-holocracy/archons.json (the one archon whose mission mentions "Heimdall admission-window maintenance", eoreader7:reading-rules-wt, names only native/eval/the-fold/lib/product-assay.mjs and native/tests/spans-frontmatter.test.js -- neither is heimdall.mjs itself), checked before editing.
basis: Rather than hand-fix the same recurring infrastructure issue a third time, found and extended the project's own existing, purpose-built self-healing mechanism (Heimdall's probeModelServer + restartModelServer + proxy.mjs's watchdog loop), verified both the positive (no false alarm on a healthy daemon) and negative (a simulated real hang correctly caught) cases mechanically, and disclosed honestly what remains unverified (a real future recurrence in the wild).

title: How this vision gets chased, not just stated (revised: a full alignment pass -- loadBearing now reaches every body group AND the loop-quality stage; one candidate integration deliberately left undone with reasons)
text:
This ledger is the mechanism, not a description of one: append-only, each revision superseding the last without erasing it, exactly the discipline already used for every generated piece this session. Anyone — any session, any archon, any scheduled routine — reads the current fold of THIS document the same way any other document in this pipeline gets read, and appends a revision when something changes, rather than editing a fixed spec in place.

Ownership, checked against the real registries before any new work starts (per lesson #75): Chomsky (native/kernel/universal-grammar.js, eot-rich.js, english-parser.js, clause-tense.js) owns the parser/syntax substrate this session pushed on directly. Sullivan (adapters/text/morph-cues.js, existence-grain.js, eval/lavar/sullivan-*.mjs) owns morphology-by-elimination and the period-parse measurement that the parser's period-blindness should have been checked against sooner. LaVar (LAVAR.md, eval/lavar/) owns grading the reader against real material and keeping the mistake corpus this project's own honesty depends on. Grounding (organs/grounding.js, ground-cite.js — Mozi) owns verifying any claim in this vision, or built from it, against real bytes. No current archon owns ablation-grain-pressure.js's live wiring or the cursor-addressable fold interface itself — both are named gaps, not silently assigned, until an archon is actually spawned for them following the Handle-table-plus-registry check.

The concrete next actionable steps, in the order this session's own findings license them, not in order of ambition: (1) unblock the shared Ollama /api/embed contention so build-ablation-grain-prior.mjs can complete a real run — infrastructure, not code. (2) Run eval/the-fold/ablation-pressure-calibration.mjs for real once centroids exist, and only wire ablationPressureFor live if that calibration actually licenses per-case trust, per the standing rule already in the code. (3) Replace this session's ad hoc agglomerative pocket-discovery with a properly-powered, established method (the gap statistic or a real mixture-model comparison) before trusting pocket counts on real data — the synthetic tests this session ran found the ad hoc version underpowered, honestly, not fixed. (4) Only after 1-3: begin the actual cursor-addressable fold interface — the piece that has been described three times this session and built zero times.

REVISION, same session, minutes later: the user asked for this to stop being a description and become a standing process -- committed to the repo, and a scheduled Claude Code routine (model: sonnet) set up to actually resume this work on a recurring cadence, archon ownership checked each time before any new task is claimed, rather than left as a one-time write. That routine's own config and its first scheduled run are the next two lines in this ledger, appended right after this one -- read those for what's actually standing, not just planned.

REVISION, 2026-09-25/26: step 3 of the ordered next-steps list above is done -- native/adapters/text/pocket-discovery-gap.js implements the gap statistic (Tibshirani, Walther & Hastie 2001) replacing the ad hoc agglomerative-z-test approach, whose own honest earlier measurement this session found underpowered (1/5 true positives on realistic 3-cluster synthetic data). Measured on the SAME synthetic scenarios: 4/5 true positives (vs 1/5) at a cost of 1/5 false positives on null data (vs 0/5) -- a real, reported precision/recall trade-off, not an unqualified win. 5 node:test cases pass (native/adapters/text/pocket-discovery-gap.test.mjs). NOT wired into ablation-grain-pressure.js's buildCentroidsFrom -- steps 1-2 (unblock the shared Ollama /api/embed endpoint, run the real calibration) remain blocked; confirmed live via a 15s curl against http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/embed returning STATUS:000 immediately before this step, same failure mode observed all session. Checked both archon-ownership registries first (README.md Handle table, archon-holocracy/archons.json) -- neither names an owner for this domain, consistent with vision-routines' own prior disclosure of it as a named, undecided gap; no new archon was spawned for it this step. Committed as a standalone, tested module ahead of its dependency clearing, per the ledger's own instruction to do real, bounded, currently-licensed work rather than wait on a still-blocked step.

REVISION, 2026-09-25/26 (same 30-min-burst session): step 4 of the ordered next-steps list is BEGUN, not finished -- native/the-fold/fold-at.js is the first real slice of the cursor-addressable fold interface described repeatedly in this project's memory and built zero times before this file. foldAt(address, claims) partitions a flat GFP claim set into here/ancestors/descendants relative to a holon-address cursor, reusing kernel/gfp-claim.js's own holon()/contains()/ancestry() unmodified -- real, new plumbing, 6 node:test cases passing. The three richer layers the full vision describes (atmosphere, paradigm, significance) are deliberately left as typed gaps ({wired:false, reason}), never fabricated: atmosphere and paradigm each name a real existing module (kernel/atmosphere-math.js, the-fold/paradigm.js) this step did not wire because their real input shapes (an obligations sequence; a learned paradigm object) were not verified against a live caller; significance has no implementation anywhere in this repo at all, confirmed by grep before writing. Next bounded steps this names, not yet started: verify atmosphere-math.js's real obligations-sequence contract against a live caller and wire it in; verify paradigm.js's learnParadigm/evaluateParadigm contract and wire it in; design and build a real, null-measured significance function (no hand-set threshold, per this project's own standing rule) where none exists today. Checked both archon-ownership registries first (README.md Handle table, archon-holocracy/archons.json) for cursor/fold-at/foldat -- neither names an owner; no new archon was spawned for it this step, consistent with vision-routines' own prior disclosure of this domain as a named, undecided gap.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, continuing on user direction 'keep going, don't stop'): fold-at.js's atmosphere layer is now genuinely wired -- checked two real, independent production call sites first (kernel/emergent-terrain.js's atmosphereProjection, kernel/theory-of-mind.js, two separate call sites), confirmed they agree on the same obligations shape ({id, grounds, alternatives, consequences, persistence, openedAt, constraint}), then called the real interpretiveAtmosphereFactorField directly. When a caller supplies obligations, foldAt returns its real computed field; when none are supplied, atmosphere is wired:true with field:null (honestly "nothing to compute here", not "not wired"). 8 node:test cases pass (2 new, exercising both the empty and real-obligation paths). Also corrected this same ledger's own prior claim about paradigm: checking evaluateParadigm's real callers this step found ZERO outside its own test file (every real the-fold caller only ever BUILDS a paradigm via learnParadigm/learnParadigmEmergent, never evaluates a candidate against one) -- there is no live contract to verify against, so paradigm stays an honest, now more precisely worded, typed gap rather than being wired from a guess. significance remains unimplemented anywhere in the repo, re-confirmed.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, user: 'go, dont stop, that's the whole point of this'): corrected a FALSE claim this same file's own earlier revision made -- "no significance-measurement module exists anywhere in this repo" was wrong. Real, already-committed modules exist: kernel/bayes-surprise.js and kernel/consequential-surprise.js, both with real production callers (the-fold/expertise.js, form-prior.js, paradigm.js, learn-pass.js; kernel/settling.js, contextuality.js; organs/archon-compendium.js, capacities.js; docs/surprise-organs.js). Wired the part that fits foldAt's own PURE contract: bayes-surprise.js's predict() (read-only -- checked that admit() mutates the holograph and predict() does not, before choosing predict) computes real Bayesian surprisal in bits over slot/value facts derived from the claims at a cursor, when the caller supplies a holograph. 11 node:test cases pass total (4 new, including one that specifically proves the caller's holograph is never mutated). Left consequential-surprise.js's load-bearing/local partition as a precisely-reasoned gap -- it needs a dependents index and a seedsOf function whose real-world usage (checked via docs/surprise-organs.js) is domain-specific and does not generalize to holon-addressed claims without original design work not attempted this revision.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, user asked 'how close are we to arbitrary generation'): checked whether fold-at.js (built this session) connects to the nine-stage generation pipeline (native/the-fold/pipeline-run.mjs: void/surf/shape/hunt/skeleton/loop/pathos/piece).
