 - arrange.js: extended the existing loadBearingOf closure to every bodySlots entry (previously only thesisCandidates had it), combining each group's own per-statement results honestly -- true if any statement is load-bearing, null only when every one is null (nothing checkable), false otherwise, never a guessed false. Verified live against real content (native/the-fold/fixtures/cumberland-ground.md): a genuine, honest mix across 7 body groups -- 4 true, 3 false, matching the real claim structure, not a stub.
 - loop-check.js: measurePiece gains one new optional, purely-passthrough parameter (loadBearing, default null) and returns it unchanged; loopLine discloses it on the ledger only when non-null, so every existing caller's output is byte-identical to before. pipeline-run.mjs's checkLoop now supplies the real outline.thesis.loadBearing value on every call. Verified live: the real pipeline's own ledger now reads "thesis load-bearing: true" inside its loop-check output, not just inside arrange's own line.

judgeLoop's own comparison logic (carried/answered/licensed) was read but not touched -- this remains informational disclosure, matching every prior loadBearing decision this session. Re-ran the full relevant test suite after all three edits: 63/63 (arrange-loadbearing, arrange-falsify, fold-at, claim-dependencies, claims-from-feat, cli/fold-at) plus 5/5 (loop-check-falsify) passing, no regressions.

No archon dispute: arrange.js, loop-check.js, and pipeline-run.mjs are named by no archon in README.md's Handle table or archon-holocracy/archons.json, checked before editing.

Still open, honestly: the two largest forks named two cycles ago (reconciling proxy-runner.mjs's separate essay-fold.js generation system with this pipeline; building an actual narrative-fiction mode) remain untouched -- this cycle's "alignment" was scoped to the loadBearing signal's own reach inside the ALREADY-existing nine-stage pipeline, not a claim that the two separate generation systems are now reconciled.
basis: A parallel, evidence-based survey (not assumption) distinguished a real, closable integration gap (loadBearing's reach inside the existing pipeline) from a merely-plausible one that the project's own prior measurement already argues against (pocket-discovery into an uncalibrated module) -- did the former, for real, verified live; explicitly declined the latter with a stated, evidence-backed reason rather than silently skipping it.

title: How this vision gets chased, not just stated (revised: falsified loadBearing's generalization across registers on real, new content -- two distinct real gaps found, neither fixed yet)
text:
This ledger is the mechanism, not a description of one: append-only, each revision superseding the last without erasing it, exactly the discipline already used for every generated piece this session. Anyone — any session, any archon, any scheduled routine — reads the current fold of THIS document the same way any other document in this pipeline gets read, and appends a revision when something changes, rather than editing a fixed spec in place.

Ownership, checked against the real registries before any new work starts (per lesson #75): Chomsky (native/kernel/universal-grammar.js, eot-rich.js, english-parser.js, clause-tense.js) owns the parser/syntax substrate this session pushed on directly. Sullivan (adapters/text/morph-cues.js, existence-grain.js, eval/lavar/sullivan-*.mjs) owns morphology-by-elimination and the period-parse measurement that the parser's period-blindness should have been checked against sooner. LaVar (LAVAR.md, eval/lavar/) owns grading the reader against real material and keeping the mistake corpus this project's own honesty depends on. Grounding (organs/grounding.js, ground-cite.js — Mozi) owns verifying any claim in this vision, or built from it, against real bytes. No current archon owns ablation-grain-pressure.js's live wiring or the cursor-addressable fold interface itself — both are named gaps, not silently assigned, until an archon is actually spawned for them following the Handle-table-plus-registry check.

The concrete next actionable steps, in the order this session's own findings license them, not in order of ambition: (1) unblock the shared Ollama /api/embed contention so build-ablation-grain-prior.mjs can complete a real run — infrastructure, not code. (2) Run eval/the-fold/ablation-pressure-calibration.mjs for real once centroids exist, and only wire ablationPressureFor live if that calibration actually licenses per-case trust, per the standing rule already in the code. (3) Replace this session's ad hoc agglomerative pocket-discovery with a properly-powered, established method (the gap statistic or a real mixture-model comparison) before trusting pocket counts on real data — the synthetic tests this session ran found the ad hoc version underpowered, honestly, not fixed. (4) Only after 1-3: begin the actual cursor-addressable fold interface — the piece that has been described three times this session and built zero times.

REVISION, same session, minutes later: the user asked for this to stop being a description and become a standing process -- committed to the repo, and a scheduled Claude Code routine (model: sonnet) set up to actually resume this work on a recurring cadence, archon ownership checked each time before any new task is claimed, rather than left as a one-time write. That routine's own config and its first scheduled run are the next two lines in this ledger, appended right after this one -- read those for what's actually standing, not just planned.

REVISION, 2026-09-25/26: step 3 of the ordered next-steps list above is done -- native/adapters/text/pocket-discovery-gap.js implements the gap statistic (Tibshirani, Walther & Hastie 2001) replacing the ad hoc agglomerative-z-test approach, whose own honest earlier measurement this session found underpowered (1/5 true positives on realistic 3-cluster synthetic data). Measured on the SAME synthetic scenarios: 4/5 true positives (vs 1/5) at a cost of 1/5 false positives on null data (vs 0/5) -- a real, reported precision/recall trade-off, not an unqualified win. 5 node:test cases pass (native/adapters/text/pocket-discovery-gap.test.mjs). NOT wired into ablation-grain-pressure.js's buildCentroidsFrom -- steps 1-2 (unblock the shared Ollama /api/embed endpoint, run the real calibration) remain blocked; confirmed live via a 15s curl against http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/embed returning STATUS:000 immediately before this step, same failure mode observed all session. Checked both archon-ownership registries first (README.md Handle table, archon-holocracy/archons.json) -- neither names an owner for this domain, consistent with vision-routines' own prior disclosure of it as a named, undecided gap; no new archon was spawned for it this step. Committed as a standalone, tested module ahead of its dependency clearing, per the ledger's own instruction to do real, bounded, currently-licensed work rather than wait on a still-blocked step.

REVISION, 2026-09-25/26 (same 30-min-burst session): step 4 of the ordered next-steps list is BEGUN, not finished -- native/the-fold/fold-at.js is the first real slice of the cursor-addressable fold interface described repeatedly in this project's memory and built zero times before this file. foldAt(address, claims) partitions a flat GFP claim set into here/ancestors/descendants relative to a holon-address cursor, reusing kernel/gfp-claim.js's own holon()/contains()/ancestry() unmodified -- real, new plumbing, 6 node:test cases passing. The three richer layers the full vision describes (atmosphere, paradigm, significance) are deliberately left as typed gaps ({wired:false, reason}), never fabricated: atmosphere and paradigm each name a real existing module (kernel/atmosphere-math.js, the-fold/paradigm.js) this step did not wire because their real input shapes (an obligations sequence; a learned paradigm object) were not verified against a live caller; significance has no implementation anywhere in this repo at all, confirmed by grep before writing. Next bounded steps this names, not yet started: verify atmosphere-math.js's real obligations-sequence contract against a live caller and wire it in; verify paradigm.js's learnParadigm/evaluateParadigm contract and wire it in; design and build a real, null-measured significance function (no hand-set threshold, per this project's own standing rule) where none exists today. Checked both archon-ownership registries first (README.md Handle table, archon-holocracy/archons.json) for cursor/fold-at/foldat -- neither names an owner; no new archon was spawned for it this step, consistent with vision-routines' own prior disclosure of this domain as a named, undecided gap.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, continuing on user direction 'keep going, don't stop'): fold-at.js's atmosphere layer is now genuinely wired -- checked two real, independent production call sites first (kernel/emergent-terrain.js's atmosphereProjection, kernel/theory-of-mind.js, two separate call sites), confirmed they agree on the same obligations shape ({id, grounds, alternatives, consequences, persistence, openedAt, constraint}), then called the real interpretiveAtmosphereFactorField directly. When a caller supplies obligations, foldAt returns its real computed field; when none are supplied, atmosphere is wired:true with field:null (honestly "nothing to compute here", not "not wired"). 8 node:test cases pass (2 new, exercising both the empty and real-obligation paths). Also corrected this same ledger's own prior claim about paradigm: checking evaluateParadigm's real callers this step found ZERO outside its own test file (every real the-fold caller only ever BUILDS a paradigm via learnParadigm/learnParadigmEmergent, never evaluates a candidate against one) -- there is no live contract to verify against, so paradigm stays an honest, now more precisely worded, typed gap rather than being wired from a guess. significance remains unimplemented anywhere in the repo, re-confirmed.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, user: 'go, dont stop, that's the whole point of this'): corrected a FALSE claim this same file's own earlier revision made -- "no significance-measurement module exists anywhere in this repo" was wrong. Real, already-committed modules exist: kernel/bayes-surprise.js and kernel/consequential-surprise.js, both with real production callers (the-fold/expertise.js, form-prior.js, paradigm.js, learn-pass.js; kernel/settling.js, contextuality.js; organs/archon-compendium.js, capacities.js; docs/surprise-organs.js). Wired the part that fits foldAt's own PURE contract: bayes-surprise.js's predict() (read-only -- checked that admit() mutates the holograph and predict() does not, before choosing predict) computes real Bayesian surprisal in bits over slot/value facts derived from the claims at a cursor, when the caller supplies a holograph. 11 node:test cases pass total (4 new, including one that specifically proves the caller's holograph is never mutated). Left consequential-surprise.js's load-bearing/local partition as a precisely-reasoned gap -- it needs a dependents index and a seedsOf function whose real-world usage (checked via docs/surprise-organs.js) is domain-specific and does not generalize to holon-addressed claims without original design work not attempted this revision.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, user asked 'how close are we to arbitrary generation'): checked whether fold-at.js (built this session) connects to the nine-stage generation pipeline (native/the-fold/pipeline-run.mjs: void/surf/shape/hunt/skeleton/loop/pathos/piece). It does not -- confirmed by grep for any import of fold-at.js or any call to foldAt( anywhere under native/ outside fold-at.js and its own test file: zero matches, after catching and redoing a sloppier first grep that had produced a false hit on an unrelated function (proposition-holograph.js's foldAtom).

Looked for the most likely real integration point: hunt.js's huntGround(), since its name suggested it might already work with GFP-style ground addresses. It does not -- huntGround's "ground" is a different, unrelated concept (evidentiary source material admitted by topical relevance: naming a being of the subject, or carrying a topic word), a false friend of gfp-claim.js's holon-path "ground" that foldAt addresses. Wiring foldAt into the pipeline on the strength of shared terminology alone would have been exactly the guessed-composition mistake this session has repeatedly caught itself making and corrected (paradigm's contract, significance's non-existence claim) -- so it was not attempted. Real integration requires reading each pipeline stage's actual data model to find where a genuine holon-addressed claim set already exists or naturally could, which this step did not have room to do carefully. Named as the concrete next step, not guessed at: before wiring foldAt into generation, first identify which pipeline stage (if any) already produces or consumes GFP claims with real holon grounds, as opposed to the pipeline's own paragraph/text-based addressing.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, continuing 'keep going'): the prior revision correctly found hunt.js's "ground" was a false friend, but searched too narrowly before concluding no real integration point exists. Widening the check (grep for gfp-claim.js usage across every stage file pipeline-run.mjs imports) found one: native/the-fold/arrange.js imports renderGeneralization from kernel/gfp-claim.js, and arrange.js itself imports thesisBasin/thesisGeneralization from native/the-fold/thesis-claim.js -- which is the real source. thesis-claim.js builds real GFP claims with genuine holon grounds keyed to the piece's own structure: `claimFromTriple(note.end1, rel, note.end2, { ground: holon(\`/\${f.pt.part}\`), ... })` (line 136) -- one holon address per piece-part, exactly the addressing scheme foldAt consumes, not a false friend this time: verified by reading the actual line, not inferred from a name. This is confirmed, not yet wired -- thesisGen.claims is a real, holon-addressed claim set that a real caller (arrange.js) already holds at generation time; foldAt(someCursor, thesisGen.claims) would be a genuine, non-guessed integration once arrange.js's own ~650-line control flow is read carefully enough to find the right place to call it and use the result for something real (not a decorative addition). That careful read is the concrete next step, named rather than rushed into within this same burst.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, same 'keep going' thread): reading arrange.js's own actual control flow (not just its imports) around thesisGeneralization found a real, important caveat to the immediately prior revision. arrange.js's own comments report: "Measured 2026-09-25 across NINE real grounds — a house doc, two UD treebank READMEs, an OHS audit, a Call of the Wild excerpt, UK legislation, a SCOTUS oral-argument excerpt, the surf white paper, the Cumberland essay: zero basins validate" and, restated later in the same file, "Measured 2026-09-25 across nine real grounds (above): zero basins fired." The thesis-generalization branch that produces holon-grounded GFP claims (thesis-claim.js) is real code with a real, verified contract, but is ALSO measured, by this repo's own prior work, to never actually activate on the nine real documents tested so far. Wiring foldAt to thesisGen.claims would be technically correct and would still be honest, verified plumbing -- but by the repo's own numbers it would have nothing to act on in the overwhelming majority of real runs. This is not a reason to abandon the integration (the mechanism firing is itself measured, not assumed broken -- refrains DO trigger it per the same comments), but it tempers "found the real integration point" into "found a real, rarely-populated one" -- an honest correction, not a reversal. No wiring was attempted this revision; the next step is unchanged (arrange.js's full control flow, read carefully) but now carries this caveat forward rather than an unqualified "this is the answer."

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, step chosen per the ledger's own named next-step): built native/the-fold/arrange.js's claimsFromFeat(feat), the general bridge from arrangeEssay's own always-run per-point extraction (feat, notesOf -- run over EVERY point in EVERY arrangeEssay call, unconditionally, verified by reading points' construction) to real, holon-addressed GFP claims, superseding the near-dormant thesis-generalization path as the practical integration point. Reuses notesOf's own already-computed subject/relation/object triples and declared polarity via claimFromTriple; notes with notesOf's own unresolved ('?') polarity state are excluded and counted separately, never coerced into a guessed '+'/'-' (gfpClaim's own validation only accepts those two, checked against its source). A pure addition -- no existing line in arrange.js changed. 6 new tests pass, including a genuine cross-file end-to-end check (claimsFromFeat's own output fed directly into the real foldAt(), confirming a parent-part claim surfaces as an ancestor for a child cursor) -- not mocked, not asserted, run. Full existing test suites (arrange-falsify.test.mjs's 32 cases, fold-at.test.mjs's 11) re-run and still pass: this addition changed nothing else. Re-tested Ollama at the top of this cycle: still STATUS:000, steps 1-2 remain blocked. Checked both archon-ownership registries for arrange.js before touching it: neither names an owner. The concrete next step this names: run claimsFromFeat against a REAL arrangeEssay call on real material (not just synthetic feat shapes) to measure how often it actually produces claims on real documents, the way thesis-claim.js's own dormancy was measured -- not yet done this revision.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, the exact next step obs:12 named): ran claimsFromFeat against REAL arrangeEssay output on real prose, not synthetic feat shapes, through the actual pipeline (buildDraft/attachReferents/loadEotParser/attachEot/arrangeEssay). Measured on three real documents already used in this session's own summarization pilot: gpgp.md (Wikipedia, informational) 31 claims from 52 points, 0 unresolved; gift-of-the-magi.md (O. Henry, narrative) 58 claims from 140 points, 3 unresolved; war-and-peace-ch45.md (Tolstoy, translated 19th-century prose) 14 claims from 44 points, 1 unresolved. All three real, nonzero, non-degenerate -- confirming claimsFromFeat is commonly populated on real material, the opposite of thesis-claim.js's own measured zero-activation result. Exposed claimsFromFeat's output on arrangeEssay's own return value (a new `claims` key, additive only -- checked for any deep-equality assertion against a whole outline object anywhere in the repo before adding it; none found) so a real caller can reach it without reaching into arrangeEssay's function-local `feat`. Locked in as a committed, reproducible test (claims-from-feat-real.test.mjs, a real public-domain excerpt embedded directly rather than depending on this session's own scratchpad paths, unlike the pre-existing native/eval/the-fold/drive-summary-experiment.mjs's own default file paths -- a fragility noted, not fixed, this revision). Full existing suites re-verified: 44 tests across arrange-falsify.test.mjs, claims-from-feat.test.mjs and fold-at.test.mjs still pass. Re-tested Ollama at the top of this cycle: still STATUS:000, steps 1-2 remain blocked. The concrete next step this names: something must actually CALL arrangeEssay's new claims field and DO something with it via foldAt (atmosphere/significance) that changes what the pipeline produces -- until then this is verified, reachable data, not yet a capability.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing): before wiring foldAt's output into anything that shapes generated text (obs:13's own named next step), tried calling foldAt against the real claims measured last cycle to see what it actually returns. Found ancestors:0, descendants:0 for every real cursor tried against gpgp.md's 31 claims -- the ground claimsFromFeat builds, holon(`/${f.pt.part}`), is FLAT (e.g. '/p18'), so every claim sits as a sibling of every other at the same depth; foldAt's ancestor/descendant machinery had nothing to find, regardless of how much real content existed. Checked eot-draft.js's own point construction (line 187) and found every point already carries a real, pre-existing hierarchical `path` field (`whole/p${i+1}/${j+1}`, e.g. 'whole/p4/3') that arrange.js's own points construction (line 121, `{...pt, part: p.id}`) already preserves onto every feat entry as `f.pt.path` -- unused until now. Fixed: claimsFromFeat's ground is now `holon(f.pt.path ?? \`/${f.pt.part}\`)`, using the real hierarchy with a fallback for any caller whose feat entries lack `path`. Re-ran the same live inspection against gpgp.md: grounds are now genuinely nested ('/whole/p13/3', '/whole/p16/2', ...), confirmed real, not just plausible-looking.

Disclosed, not solved: even with the real hierarchy, ancestors/descendants for a point-level cursor remain empty in this design, because no claim is currently grounded at the coarser part ('/whole/pN') or whole-document level -- points are real siblings under a shared part, not ancestor/descendant of each other, and foldAt has no separate "siblings" category. Getting real ancestor context (not just a correct address) needs either claims at multiple granularities or a sibling-aware fourth category in foldAt itself -- named as the next concrete step, not attempted this revision. 2 new tests lock in the fix (path used when present; flat fallback unchanged when absent); full suite re-verified at 47/47 passing across claims-from-feat, claims-from-feat-real, arrange-falsify and fold-at test files. Re-tested Ollama at the top of this cycle: still down, steps 1-2 remain blocked.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, the exact gap obs:14 named): added a fourth, purely structural category to foldAt -- siblings: claims sharing the cursor's own parent holon (one level up, via gfp-claim.js's own already-exported segmentsOf/holon, no new addressing concept). This directly answers what obs:14 found and disclosed: real per-point claims from claimsFromFeat are true siblings of each other under a shared part, not ancestor/descendant, and foldAt had no category for that relationship. Re-ran the same live inspection against gpgp.md's real claims that found the original gap: a cursor at /whole/p16/2 now correctly returns /whole/p16/1 as a real sibling -- confirmed on real data, not just the synthetic fixture. parentOf(h) returns null for the root ('/' has no parent), so the root cursor correctly has zero siblings, a real structural fact rather than an arbitrary special case. 3 new tests added (sibling inclusion, no double-counting an ancestor as a sibling, root has zero siblings); full suite re-verified at 49/49 passing across fold-at, claims-from-feat, claims-from-feat-real and arrange-falsify test files. Re-tested Ollama at the top of this cycle: still down, steps 1-2 remain blocked. The concrete next step this names: foldAt now has real, populated here/ancestors/siblings on real material -- the next honest question is whether wiring this into a generation-shaping stage (finish.js, loop-check.js) actually improves anything measurable, since no existing gap in either file currently names a use for it (checked two cycles ago); that measurement, not another foldAt feature, is what's actually owed next.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, pursuing obs:15's own named question): before writing more foldAt code, tried to find a REAL, already-motivated use for its siblings/ancestors in a generation-shaping stage, rather than inventing one. Read three candidate files' actual logic (not just names or comments): hunt.js's huntGround (already found, two cycles ago, to be a false-friend "ground" concept -- evidentiary source material, unrelated); finish.js's takesUp (checks whether a part's opening sentence "takes up" a being or word from the previous part's closing sentence -- works entirely through referent resolution and word overlap on raw text, never touches a GFP claim); loop-check.js's measurePiece/judgeLoop (measures whether a loop preserved anchors and answered the task's questions -- works through anchorsFor/carries on the piece's own text, never a GFP claim either). None of the three has an unmet need that foldAt's holon-addressed claim context would fill; each already solves its own adjacency/coherence problem through a different, working, non-claim-based mechanism. Wiring foldAt into any of them now would be manufacturing a use for it, not fulfilling one already there -- exactly the invented-purpose mistake this session's own standing rule (measure, don't assume) exists to catch.

This is not a dead end for foldAt, but it does redirect the real next step: either (a) foldAt's value is as a genuinely NEW capability (an interactive query/inspection surface over already-generated material, not a silent improvement folded into logic that already works its own way), which has never been attempted and would need its own honest scoping, not a forced retrofit; or (b) a deliberately DESIGNED experiment -- pick one specific generation decision, build a foldAt-informed alternative, and measure it against the current approach on real material -- which is a real, bounded project of its own, not something to back into by searching existing files for an accidental fit. Which of these two paths is worth pursuing is an open decision this revision names but does not make.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, pursuing obs:16's own named option (a)): built cli/fold-at.mjs, the first time anything in this repo lets a person actually run a command and ask "what is the fold at this point" of a real document, rather than only exercising the backend through a test or a throwaway script. Runs the real pipeline (buildDraft, attachReferents, loadEotParser, attachEot, arrangeEssay) on a file argument, then the real foldAt(address, outline.claims), printing here/ancestors/siblings/descendants and each layer's real state -- a computed field when wired, the exact honest gap reason string when not, never a fabricated summary. A `list` address mode prints every real distinct holon address the document actually produced, so a user finds a real cursor rather than guessing one. Verified against a real document (gpgp.md): 31 claims, 31 addresses listed correctly; querying /whole/p16/2 correctly returned its real sibling at /whole/p16/1 and honest gap text for significance and paradigm. 3 process-level tests (spawning the real CLI, not importing its internals) lock this in, covering usage/exit-2, list mode, and a real address query's full output shape. This is the "genuinely new capability" path named as option (a) two cycles ago, chosen over forcing a retrofit into pipeline stages already found to have no motivating gap for it.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing): the CLI's significance output previously always printed "gap: no holograph supplied" since nothing built one. Fixed: cli/fold-at.mjs now builds a real bayes-surprise.js holograph, admitting (via the real, documented-mutating admit()) every OTHER claim in the document (excluding the queried cursor's own, to avoid a self-fulfilling low score), using the same slotsFromClaims() shape foldAt itself already uses internally (exported from fold-at.js for this purpose -- a one-word, no-behavior-change export). foldAt then reports the cursor's real surprisal against this real, document-derived prior via its own existing predict()-only path (never re-admitting).

Honestly measured, not just built: tested against gpgp.md's 4 different real cursors -- significance came back as either 16.54 or 17.54 bits, only two distinct values across four tries. The likely cause, checked by reading slotsFromClaims' own slot-naming: every claim's role fillers compete in the SAME small set of shared slots (rel, role:ARG0, role:ARG1, polarity) across the whole 31-claim document, and most specific fillers (proper nouns, specific nouns) are unique to the document, so the "novel value" cost in bayes-surprise.js's own Bayesian model dominates almost uniformly regardless of which claim is queried. This is a real, working number, not fabricated -- but it does not yet meaningfully discriminate "surprising" from "unsurprising" content on a corpus this small, and should not be presented as more informative than it is. 2 new tests (fold-at.js's export, the CLI's real-number output) plus the full existing suite re-verified passing (16 fold-at + 4 cli tests). Re-tested Ollama: still down.

The next honest question this names: does significance become more discriminating on a larger real document (war-and-peace-ch45.md, or the full text rather than an excerpt), or is a coarser slot design (grouping by relation LEMMA across claims, not per-claim-instance) needed regardless of size -- not yet tested, named as the next step rather than assumed either way.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, resolving the exact question obs:18 named): tested cli/fold-at.mjs's significance output against a larger real document (gift-of-the-magi.md, 58 claims) instead of the smaller one (gpgp.md, 31 claims) that showed only two distinct values (16.54/17.54 bits) last cycle. Sampled 10 real cursors: significance spanned 11.51 to 19.83 bits, an 8.3-bit range -- genuine variance, not a constant. Checked causally, not just numerically: the lowest-scoring cursor ("she do it", 11.51 bits) uses common pronoun/verb words repeated throughout the story; the highest-scoring cursor ("hair fall rippling", 19.83 bits) uses distinctive, unique descriptive words -- exactly the expected Bayesian-surprise behavior (common = unsurprising = low bits, rare = surprising = high bits). This resolves the open question: the near-constant values measured last cycle were a real corpus-size effect (a 31-claim document has too few repeated relations/fillers for the prior to differentiate against), not a flaw in the slot design -- no code change was needed or made this revision, only the measurement itself, which the ledger's own last revision correctly identified as the thing actually owed.

The concrete next step this leaves open: significance is now confirmed real, working, and meaningfully discriminating on real material of sufficient size -- the same three named gaps from earlier revisions remain unaddressed (paradigm has no live caller to verify against; consequential-surprise's load-bearing/local partition needs a seedsOf design for holon-addressed claims; foldAt has never been tried on a document larger than ~140 points). Any of these, or a genuinely new direction, remains open for the next cycle -- none is uniquely licensed by this revision's own finding.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (scheduled cron firing, picking one of the three open options from obs:19 -- consequential-surprise.js's own named gap): built native/the-fold/claim-dependencies.js, the missing seedsOf/dependents-index design for wiring kernel/consequential-surprise.js's load-bearing/local significance partition into holon-addressed GFP claims. Before building, checked ownership carefully and found a real, non-obvious false-friend: an archon's mission mentions "cascade," but its own text names native/kernel/prior-query.js's unrelated "meaning-potential cascade" (a chain of prior-family lookups), not kernel/cascade.js (BFS reachability over a dependency graph) -- confirmed by reading prior-query.js directly; kernel/cascade.js itself has zero references in either registry, genuinely unowned.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (user: "keep improving" -> "wire it in so it works from all surfaces"): a real, grep-verified check found that proxy-runner.mjs (the file backing the live chat/TUI/API surface the user actually uses daily) does NOT call pipeline-run.mjs, arrangeEssay, skeletonLoop, or foldAt anywhere -- it composes essays through a wholly separate, independently-evolved system (the-fold/essay-fold.js's wideToAtoms/foldWideToShape/beatsFromGround, a string-keyword claim-identity mechanism with its own FOLD_CLAIM_VARIANTS/FOLD_STOP/FOLD_VERBS word lists), deeply integrated with the live session's streaming (onThinking/onNote), citation ledger, and its own gap-redraw loop -- machinery pipeline-run.mjs's own runPipeline has no equivalent for. This is not a small wiring gap: it is two mature, independently-built generation systems that have never been reconciled. Asked the user for direction before touching the live daily-use system given the size and risk; user chose full integration, then, on seeing the live system's actual depth (streaming hooks, citation ledger, gap-redraw), redirected: chase a concrete, harder test first -- a short story inspired by a true story, grounded but fictional -- rather than force an unreviewed architectural merge in one sitting.

Ran that real test on native/the-fold/fixtures/cumberland-ground.md (the real, factual 1779-1780 Donelson flotilla founding of Nashville) through the standalone pipeline-run.mjs with a fiction-oriented task. RESULT, honest: the pipeline does NOT produce narrative fiction -- no characters acting, no scenes, no dialogue, no invented-but-licensed departure from the source. It produces embellished, more lyrical EXPOSITION of the same source sentences ("its very soul," "a testament to," "the city's lifeblood") -- confirmed on two independent runs. This is a real, structural finding: arrangeEssay's thesis/claims model and Gebser's own arrival gate (origin-present, nothing-lost) are built for non-fiction elaboration, not narrative departure from source structure -- fiction inherently needs invented scenes that are NOT anchored to any witnessed statement, which the current architecture has no mechanism to license. A genuine, disclosed gap toward "arbitrary generation," not attempted to close in this cycle -- it would need real design work (a distinct narrative mode, not a parameter tweak), not invented here.

A concrete, real, fixable BUG was found and fixed along the way, independent of the fiction question: the first fiction-test run's own output contained a verbatim leaked sentence -- "* **Embedded Information:** The fact about the river's length is woven into the sentence, making it more natural and informative." -- the model commenting on its own phrasing technique, in markdown bold-label formatting, inline in the finished piece. Confirmed mechanically that this is a THIRD, previously-uncovered discourse register: neither referent-verify.js's existing META_SENTENCE_RE (task-talk) nor ASSISTANT_VOICE_RE (chat-assistant voice) matched it (checked directly against both regexes with the exact leaked text, no match either way), and admission.js's own looksMeta check never ran on it because it bonded to the prior landing as a "turn," which admission.js's own documented rule (lines 507-511) exempts from the meta check -- a rule whose own stated justification ("the chain cannot start from a leak because the first leak has no prior to bond to") this exact observation falsifies. Fixed by adding one new regex to referent-verify.js's isMetaSentence, grounded in this exact verbatim leak (following the file's own stated convention: every pattern here is grounded in a real observed leak, never invented speculatively) -- a leading bullet plus a bolded label is the structural tell, checked unconditionally in prosify.js before admission.js's turn-exemption ever runs, so it closes this leak regardless of that separate, deeper question. Verified: the leak text now correctly flagged, ordinary prose (including real bolded emphasis without a leading bullet) unaffected, all 10 existing referent-verify-falsify.test.mjs tests still pass, and a full rerun of the same fiction test on the same real content no longer shows the leak. The admission.js turn-exemption rule itself is left unreviewed and unfixed -- named honestly as a real, falsified-but-unaddressed finding for a future cycle, not silently absorbed into this narrower fix.

No archon dispute: neither referent-verify.js nor proxy-runner.mjs nor essay-fold.js is named by any archon in README.md's Handle table or archon-holocracy/archons.json, checked before editing.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (re-tested Ollama fresh per standing instruction, not assumed): confirmed /api/embed was down again -- same scheduler-hang signature as before (curl exit 28 / STATUS:000; /api/tags answered 200 on the same process), on the SAME long-lived daemon process this session already fixed once, exactly the recurrence risk flagged as an open operational concern two cycles ago. Re-applied the known fix (quit the app fully, relaunch `ollama serve` directly with OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11435), verified live (a real 768-dim embedding returned in under a second). This confirms the earlier fix was a real mitigation, not a permanent cure -- a standing watchdog remains the honest long-term answer, still not built.

With embed re-confirmed working (steps 1-2 of the ordered list remain otherwise already addressed from prior cycles -- calibration already ran, result already recorded as not calibrated), used the remaining bounded step on the more substantial open item named last cycle: admission.js's turn-exemption rule, whose own comment claimed "the chain cannot start from a leak because the first leak has no prior to bond to" -- a claim last cycle's real observed leak (the 'Embedded Information' technique-commentary, fiction-test-1) already falsified, since that leak bonded as a turn to an ordinary preceding sentence, not to a prior leak. Investigated whether to remove the exemption outright and found a real, currently-passing test (admission-falsify.test.mjs, "a turn whose connectives are scaffold words is admitted on motion, not refused as meta") that depends on this exemption for a genuine, legitimate case -- removing it blind would have broken tested, correct behavior to fix a comment's overclaim rather than an active exploit (the specific leak that motivated this is already closed at an earlier gate, referent-verify.js's isMetaSentence, which runs unconditionally before this exemption is ever reached). Corrected the comment to state the narrower, honest truth instead: the exemption remains necessary for a real tested case, its original blanket justification is disproven by a real counterexample, and that counterexample's exploit is closed elsewhere, not by this exemption. Comment-only, no behavior change -- verified by re-running admission-falsify.test.mjs and referent-verify-falsify.test.mjs (41/41 passing, unchanged from before this edit).

No archon dispute: admission.js is named by no archon in README.md's Handle table or archon-holocracy/archons.json, checked before editing.

Still open, honestly: whether admission.js's looksMeta call should ALSO run (not skip) for turns in some narrower form remains an unresolved design question -- doing so safely would need a second, independently-observed leak that exploits the turn exemption specifically (not yet found; the one real case is already closed elsewhere) before inventing a fix for a merely-hypothetical exploit. The two larger forks named last cycle (reconciling proxy-runner.mjs's separate generation system with this session's pipeline; building an actual narrative-fiction mode) remain untouched.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (user: "have his team fix this issue" -- Heimdall, asked about directly this turn): the last two cycles each required a manual restart of the Ollama daemon for the same recurring scheduler hang (embed requests hang indefinitely with zero bytes back, while generate and tags stay healthy). Rather than fix it by hand a third time, found the real, already-existing machinery meant for exactly this: heimdall.mjs's probeModelServer, whose own committed comment ("LESSON 22", 2026-09-21) documents discovering this SAME class of gap once before for generate ("/api/tags alone... a wedged server answers tags instantly while every generate hangs") and fixing it by adding a real generate probe. That fix was never extended to embed -- the function's own resident-model scan has always explicitly EXCLUDED embed models from its liveness check (`!/embed/i.test(...)`), so this exact failure mode has been structurally invisible to Heimdall's own watchdog (proxy.mjs's lines 2944-2953, which already restarts the model server after 3 consecutive probe failures) the whole time.

Extended probeModelServer with a real embed-liveness check, mirroring the generate probe's own pattern exactly: reads whichever model /api/tags itself reports as embedding-capable (via its real `capabilities` field -- never a hardcoded "nomic-embed-text", so this generalizes to whatever the box actually has) and attempts one minimal, strict-timeout /api/embed call; failure or timeout reports `{ ok: false, surface: "embed" }`, the same shape the existing generate-failure path already returns, so the ALREADY-EXISTING watchdog loop and restartModelServer need zero changes of their own to start catching and auto-recovering from this. Verified both directions for real: (1) against the actual live daemon right now (healthy), the new check passed cleanly with no false alarm; (2) against a fake local server built to reproduce the exact real symptom (tags/ps answer, embed never responds), the probe correctly returned `{ok:false, surface:"embed"}` under a 1.5s timeout. Re-ran the full existing Heimdall probe/fleet/self-health test suites (20/20 passing, no regressions, including the existing "an embedder alone is not a model to probe" case, confirming compatibility).

This is expected to end the need for a human (or a cron cycle) to manually diagnose and restart Ollama for this specific failure going forward -- Heimdall's own standing watchdog should now do it. Not verified: whether the watchdog actually fires correctly the NEXT time this recurs in the wild (only a simulated reproduction was tested, not a live in-the-wild catch) -- that is a real, honest limit of what could be confirmed this cycle, disclosed rather than overclaimed.

No archon dispute: heimdall.mjs is named by no archon in README.md's Handle table or archon-holocracy/archons.json (the one archon whose mission mentions "Heimdall admission-window maintenance", eoreader7:reading-rules-wt, names only native/eval/the-fold/lib/product-assay.mjs and native/tests/spans-frontmatter.test.js -- neither is heimdall.mjs itself), checked before editing.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (user: "get all the work we've been doing fully aligned with the rest of the pipeline"): ran a parallel, read-only research survey (4 agents) auditing this session's own new modules against the real pipeline fresh, rather than trusting prior reports. Findings, each independently verified with file:line citations and real command output:

(1) loadBearing was real and live in pipeline-run.mjs (pValue: 0.05 confirmed still wired, 36/36 targeted tests passing) but reached only the single thesis field -- the four thesisCandidates and the rest of the outline's body groups (bodySlots) had no such signal at all, and loop-check.js's own measurePiece/judgeLoop (the stage that decides whether a loop of the spiral "left something useful") never received it either, despite pipeline-run.mjs's checkLoop closure already having outline.thesis.loadBearing sitting in scope the whole time.

(2) pocket-discovery-gap.js's real, tested gap-statistic clustering (from a prior cycle) has exactly zero production callers -- confirmed by exhaustive grep, only its own test imports it -- and a candidate integration into ablation-grain-pressure.js's buildCentroidsFrom (which still reduces every POS to one flat mean vector, no clustering at all) was investigated and found premature: this session's own calibration test already measured that module's confidence field as uncalibrated for per-case trust (high-margin accuracy 0.171 actually LOWER than low-margin 0.220, Fisher p=0.798). Refining centroid shape would polish a signal already found unreliable rather than address the actual, still-undiagnosed reason margin doesn't track correctness. Deliberately NOT wired -- this is the correct outcome of the standing "no hand-set thresholds, measure first" discipline, not an oversight.

Closed the two real gaps found in (1), both purely additive, no behavior change to any selection or keep/undo decision:
 - arrange.js: extended the existing loadBearingOf closure to every bodySlots entry (previously only thesisCandidates had it), combining each group's own per-statement results honestly -- true if any statement is load-bearing, null only when every one is null (nothing checkable), false otherwise, never a guessed false. Verified live against real content (native/the-fold/fixtures/cumberland-ground.md): a genuine, honest mix across 7 body groups -- 4 true, 3 false, matching the real claim structure, not a stub.
 - loop-check.js: measurePiece gains one new optional, purely-passthrough parameter (loadBearing, default null) and returns it unchanged; loopLine discloses it on the ledger only when non-null, so every existing caller's output is byte-identical to before. pipeline-run.mjs's checkLoop now supplies the real outline.thesis.loadBearing value on every call. Verified live: the real pipeline's own ledger now reads "thesis load-bearing: true" inside its loop-check output, not just inside arrange's own line.

judgeLoop's own comparison logic (carried/answered/licensed) was read but not touched -- this remains informational disclosure, matching every prior loadBearing decision this session. Re-ran the full relevant test suite after all three edits: 63/63 (arrange-loadbearing, arrange-falsify, fold-at, claim-dependencies, claims-from-feat, cli/fold-at) plus 5/5 (loop-check-falsify) passing, no regressions.

No archon dispute: arrange.js, loop-check.js, and pipeline-run.mjs are named by no archon in README.md's Handle table or archon-holocracy/archons.json, checked before editing.

Still open, honestly: the two largest forks named two cycles ago (reconciling proxy-runner.mjs's separate essay-fold.js generation system with this pipeline; building an actual narrative-fiction mode) remain untouched -- this cycle's "alignment" was scoped to the loadBearing signal's own reach inside the ALREADY-existing nine-stage pipeline, not a claim that the two separate generation systems are now reconciled.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (user: "falsify it on vastly different types of prompts" -- every prior test this session used historical-narrative material, e.g. the Cumberland River fixture, never tested): ran the real, live pipeline (native/the-fold/pipeline-run.mjs, real local model) against three genuinely different, real, public-domain content types never used before this session -- a technical/procedural description (bicycle rim brake mechanics), a legal/regulatory excerpt (First Amendment jurisprudence, real case names and years), and a scientific-explanatory excerpt (photosynthesis). This is the first time this session's loadBearing signal was tested outside the narrative-historical register.

RESULT, honest and mechanically verified: the signal does NOT generalize evenly. The technical/procedural domain produced a real, non-null loadBearing:true on its own winning thesis ('Each arm holds a rubber pad.', a plain transitive SVO) -- the chain works correctly outside narrative material. But BOTH the legal and scientific domains returned loadBearing:null ('no extractable claims') on their own winning theses, and direct inspection of the real EOT parse trees found two DISTINCT, previously-unknown root causes, not one vague failure:
 (1) LEGAL -- a real structural gap in native/the-fold/arrange.js's notesOf: the winning thesis ('Freedom of speech under the First Amendment is not absolute.') was confirmed CORRECTLY parsed (root: the predicate adjective 'absolute', with real nsubj and advmod arcs) -- but notesOf requires both a subject arc AND an object/oblique arc directly off the root before emitting any note, and a predicate-adjective root has no object arc by grammatical construction. notesOf silently emits zero notes for every copular/predicate-adjective sentence ("X is Y", "X is not Y") -- a real, common, and until now undiagnosed coverage gap, not a parser problem.
 (2) SCIENCE -- a genuine EOT/UD parser root-selection error: 'Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.' is a plain transitive SVO sentence that SHOULD satisfy notesOf's own requirement, but the real parse tree rooted on the noun 'energy' instead of the verb 'converts' (arcs off the wrongly-chosen root: nsubj->Photosynthesis, compound->light, nmod->energy) -- a real parser mistake, matching this project's own already-measured parser-accuracy ceiling (gold-based retraining transferred on only 1 of 4 newly-targeted patterns, a prior session's finding), not a new defect in this session's own code.

NOT fixed this cycle, named honestly: extending notesOf to also extract copular/predicate-adjective claims (a real, moderate-sized feature addition needing its own design and test coverage, not a one-line fix) and the underlying parser's root-selection accuracy on scientific prose (matching a ceiling this project has already found expensive to move) both remain open, disclosed gaps for a future cycle -- this cycle's licensed step was the falsification itself, which the standing discipline treats as real, valuable work in its own right, not merely a precursor to a fix.

Separately, per direct user instruction this cycle: restarted proxy.mjs (the long-running daemon, up since 2026-09-23, predating the Heimdall embed-watchdog fix committed 2026-09-26 -- Node does not hot-reload, so that fix had never actually run in the live process) -- confirmed cleanly shut down and relaunched with the same topology, Heimdall's own re-forging visibly active on the fresh process (fold-8812/fold-8819 detected down and re-forged automatically in the fresh log). The user explicitly redirected away from further chasing the Ollama embed issue specifically ("i keep saying, i dont know if ollama can handle embedding and even if so we dont need it") and noted embedding, if ever needed, could be done locally or in-browser instead -- recorded here for continuity, not acted on further this cycle.

No archon dispute: arrange.js and the EOT parser are named by no archon in README.md's Handle table or archon-holocracy/archons.json, checked before this research (no code was edited this cycle, so no reason.mjs-gated write was needed beyond this ledger revision itself).
basis: A real, mechanically-verified falsification test on new, never-before-used content found the loadBearing signal's true coverage boundary: it works on verb-dense procedural prose but has two distinct, now-diagnosed gaps (a structural extraction gap for copular claims, a parser root-selection error) on legal and scientific registers -- exactly the kind of honest boundary-finding this project's own standing discipline treats as valuable, not a failure to hide.

title: How this vision gets chased, not just stated (revised: closed the copular-claim gap found last cycle; found and fixed a real, more serious determinism bug along the way)
text:
This ledger is the mechanism, not a description of one: append-only, each revision superseding the last without erasing it, exactly the discipline already used for every generated piece this session. Anyone — any session, any archon, any scheduled routine — reads the current fold of THIS document the same way any other document in this pipeline gets read, and appends a revision when something changes, rather than editing a fixed spec in place.

Ownership, checked against the real registries before any new work starts (per lesson #75): Chomsky (native/kernel/universal-grammar.js, eot-rich.js, english-parser.js, clause-tense.js) owns the parser/syntax substrate this session pushed on directly. Sullivan (adapters/text/morph-cues.js, existence-grain.js, eval/lavar/sullivan-*.mjs) owns morphology-by-elimination and the period-parse measurement that the parser's period-blindness should have been checked against sooner. LaVar (LAVAR.md, eval/lavar/) owns grading the reader against real material and keeping the mistake corpus this project's own honesty depends on. Grounding (organs/grounding.js, ground-cite.js — Mozi) owns verifying any claim in this vision, or built from it, against real bytes. No current archon owns ablation-grain-pressure.js's live wiring or the cursor-addressable fold interface itself — both are named gaps, not silently assigned, until an archon is actually spawned for them following the Handle-table-plus-registry check.

The concrete next actionable steps, in the order this session's own findings license them, not in order of ambition: (1) unblock the shared Ollama /api/embed contention so build-ablation-grain-prior.mjs can complete a real run — infrastructure, not code. (2) Run eval/the-fold/ablation-pressure-calibration.mjs for real once centroids exist, and only wire ablationPressureFor live if that calibration actually licenses per-case trust, per the standing rule already in the code. (3) Replace this session's ad hoc agglomerative pocket-discovery with a properly-powered, established method (the gap statistic or a real mixture-model comparison) before trusting pocket counts on real data — the synthetic tests this session ran found the ad hoc version underpowered, honestly, not fixed. (4) Only after 1-3: begin the actual cursor-addressable fold interface — the piece that has been described three times this session and built zero times.

REVISION, same session, minutes later: the user asked for this to stop being a description and become a standing process -- committed to the repo, and a scheduled Claude Code routine (model: sonnet) set up to actually resume this work on a recurring cadence, archon ownership checked each time before any new task is claimed, rather than left as a one-time write. That routine's own config and its first scheduled run are the next two lines in this ledger, appended right after this one -- read those for what's actually standing, not just planned.

REVISION, 2026-09-25/26: step 3 of the ordered next-steps list above is done -- native/adapters/text/pocket-discovery-gap.js implements the gap statistic (Tibshirani, Walther & Hastie 2001) replacing the ad hoc agglomerative-z-test approach, whose own honest earlier measurement this session found underpowered (1/5 true positives on realistic 3-cluster synthetic data). Measured on the SAME synthetic scenarios: 4/5 true positives (vs 1/5) at a cost of 1/5 false positives on null data (vs 0/5) -- a real, reported precision/recall trade-off, not an unqualified win. 5 node:test cases pass (native/adapters/text/pocket-discovery-gap.test.mjs). NOT wired into ablation-grain-pressure.js's buildCentroidsFrom -- steps 1-2 (unblock the shared Ollama /api/embed endpoint, run the real calibration) remain blocked; confirmed live via a 15s curl against http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/embed returning STATUS:000 immediately before this step, same failure mode observed all session. Checked both archon-ownership registries first (README.md Handle table, archon-holocracy/archons.json) -- neither names an owner for this domain, consistent with vision-routines' own prior disclosure of it as a named, undecided gap; no new archon was spawned for it this step. Committed as a standalone, tested module ahead of its dependency clearing, per the ledger's own instruction to do real, bounded, currently-licensed work rather than wait on a still-blocked step.

REVISION, 2026-09-25/26 (same 30-min-burst session): step 4 of the ordered next-steps list is BEGUN, not finished -- native/the-fold/fold-at.js is the first real slice of the cursor-addressable fold interface described repeatedly in this project's memory and built zero times before this file. foldAt(address, claims) partitions a flat GFP claim set into here/ancestors/descendants relative to a holon-address cursor, reusing kernel/gfp-claim.js's own holon()/contains()/ancestry() unmodified -- real, new plumbing, 6 node:test cases passing. The three richer layers the full vision describes (atmosphere, paradigm, significance) are deliberately left as typed gaps ({wired:false, reason}), never fabricated: atmosphere and paradigm each name a real existing module (kernel/atmosphere-math.js, the-fold/paradigm.js) this step did not wire because their real input shapes (an obligations sequence; a learned paradigm object) were not verified against a live caller; significance has no implementation anywhere in this repo at all, confirmed by grep before writing. Next bounded steps this names, not yet started: verify atmosphere-math.js's real obligations-sequence contract against a live caller and wire it in; verify paradigm.js's learnParadigm/evaluateParadigm contract and wire it in; design and build a real, null-measured significance function (no hand-set threshold, per this project's own standing rule) where none exists today. Checked both archon-ownership registries first (README.md Handle table, archon-holocracy/archons.json) for cursor/fold-at/foldat -- neither names an owner; no new archon was spawned for it this step, consistent with vision-routines' own prior disclosure of this domain as a named, undecided gap.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, continuing on user direction 'keep going, don't stop'): fold-at.js's atmosphere layer is now genuinely wired -- checked two real, independent production call sites first (kernel/emergent-terrain.js's atmosphereProjection, kernel/theory-of-mind.js, two separate call sites), confirmed they agree on the same obligations shape ({id, grounds, alternatives, consequences, persistence, openedAt, constraint}), then called the real interpretiveAtmosphereFactorField directly. When a caller supplies obligations, foldAt returns its real computed field; when none are supplied, atmosphere is wired:true with field:null (honestly "nothing to compute here", not "not wired"). 8 node:test cases pass (2 new, exercising both the empty and real-obligation paths). Also corrected this same ledger's own prior claim about paradigm: checking evaluateParadigm's real callers this step found ZERO outside its own test file (every real the-fold caller only ever BUILDS a paradigm via learnParadigm/learnParadigmEmergent, never evaluates a candidate against one) -- there is no live contract to verify against, so paradigm stays an honest, now more precisely worded, typed gap rather than being wired from a guess. significance remains unimplemented anywhere in the repo, re-confirmed.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, user: 'go, dont stop, that's the whole point of this'): corrected a FALSE claim this same file's own earlier revision made -- "no significance-measurement module exists anywhere in this repo" was wrong. Real, already-committed modules exist: kernel/bayes-surprise.js and kernel/consequential-surprise.js, both with real production callers (the-fold/expertise.js, form-prior.js, paradigm.js, learn-pass.js; kernel/settling.js, contextuality.js; organs/archon-compendium.js, capacities.js; docs/surprise-organs.js). Wired the part that fits foldAt's own PURE contract: bayes-surprise.js's predict() (read-only -- checked that admit() mutates the holograph and predict() does not, before choosing predict) computes real Bayesian surprisal in bits over slot/value facts derived from the claims at a cursor, when the caller supplies a holograph. 11 node:test cases pass total (4 new, including one that specifically proves the caller's holograph is never mutated). Left consequential-surprise.js's load-bearing/local partition as a precisely-reasoned gap -- it needs a dependents index and a seedsOf function whose real-world usage (checked via docs/surprise-organs.js) is domain-specific and does not generalize to holon-addressed claims without original design work not attempted this revision.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, user asked 'how close are we to arbitrary generation'): checked whether fold-at.js (built this session) connects to the nine-stage generation pipeline (native/the-fold/pipeline-run.mjs: void/surf/shape/hunt/skeleton/loop/pathos/piece). It does not -- confirmed by grep for any import of fold-at.js or any call to foldAt( anywhere under native/ outside fold-at.js and its own test file: zero matches, after catching and redoing a sloppier first grep that had produced a false hit on an unrelated function (proposition-holograph.js's foldAtom).

Looked for the most likely real integration point: hunt.js's huntGround(), since its name suggested it might already work with GFP-style ground addresses. It does not -- huntGround's "ground" is a different, unrelated concept (evidentiary source material admitted by topical relevance: naming a being of the subject, or carrying a topic word), a false friend of gfp-claim.js's holon-path "ground" that foldAt addresses. Wiring foldAt into the pipeline on the strength of shared terminology alone would have been exactly the guessed-composition mistake this session has repeatedly caught itself making and corrected (paradigm's contract, significance's non-existence claim) -- so it was not attempted. Real integration requires reading each pipeline stage's actual data model to find where a genuine holon-addressed claim set already exists or naturally could, which this step did not have room to do carefully. Named as the concrete next step, not guessed at: before wiring foldAt into generation, first identify which pipeline stage (if any) already produces or consumes GFP claims with real holon grounds, as opposed to the pipeline's own paragraph/text-based addressing.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, continuing 'keep going'): the prior revision correctly found hunt.js's "ground" was a false friend, but searched too narrowly before concluding no real integration point exists. Widening the check (grep for gfp-claim.js usage across every stage file pipeline-run.mjs imports) found one: native/the-fold/arrange.js imports renderGeneralization from kernel/gfp-claim.js, and arrange.js itself imports thesisBasin/thesisGeneralization from native/the-fold/thesis-claim.js -- which is the real source. thesis-claim.js builds real GFP claims with genuine holon grounds keyed to the piece's own structure: `claimFromTriple(note.end1, rel, note.end2, { ground: holon(\`/\${f.pt.part}\`), ... })` (line 136) -- one holon address per piece-part, exactly the addressing scheme foldAt consumes, not a false friend this time: verified by reading the actual line, not inferred from a name. This is confirmed, not yet wired -- thesisGen.claims is a real, holon-addressed claim set that a real caller (arrange.js) already holds at generation time; foldAt(someCursor, thesisGen.claims) would be a genuine, non-guessed integration once arrange.js's own ~650-line control flow is read carefully enough to find the right place to call it and use the result for something real (not a decorative addition). That careful read is the concrete next step, named rather than rushed into within this same burst.

REVISION, 2026-09-26 (same burst session, same 'keep going' thread): reading arrange.js's own actual control flow (not just its imports) around thesisGeneralization found a real, important caveat to the immediately prior revision. arrange.js's own comments report: "Measured 2026-09-25 across NINE real grounds — a house doc, two UD treebank READMEs, an OHS audit, a Call of the Wild excerpt, UK legislation, a SCOTUS oral-argument excerpt, the surf white paper, the Cumberland essay: zero basins validate" and, restated later in the same file, "Measured 2026-09-25 across nine real grounds (above): zero basins fired." The thesis-generalization branch that produces holon-grounded GFP claims (thesis-claim.js) is real code with a real, verified contract, but is ALSO measured, by this repo's own prior work, to never actually activate on the nine real documents tested so far. Wiring foldAt to thesisGen.claims would be technically correct and would still be honest, verified plumbing -- but by the repo's own numbers it would have nothing to act on in the overwhelming majority of real runs.  (2) SCIENCE -- a genuine EOT/UD parser root-selection error: 'Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose.' is a plain transitive SVO sentence that SHOULD satisfy notesOf's own requirement, but the real parse tree rooted on the noun 'energy' instead of the verb 'converts' (arcs off the wrongly-chosen root: nsubj->Photosynthesis, compound->light, nmod->energy) -- a real parser mistake, matching this project's own already-measured parser-accuracy ceiling (gold-based retraining transferred on only 1 of 4 newly-targeted patterns, a prior session's finding), not a new defect in this session's own code.

NOT fixed this cycle, named honestly: extending notesOf to also extract copular/predicate-adjective claims (a real, moderate-sized feature addition needing its own design and test coverage, not a one-line fix) and the underlying parser's root-selection accuracy on scientific prose (matching a ceiling this project has already found expensive to move) both remain open, disclosed gaps for a future cycle -- this cycle's licensed step was the falsification itself, which the standing discipline treats as real, valuable work in its own right, not merely a precursor to a fix.

Separately, per direct user instruction this cycle: restarted proxy.mjs (the long-running daemon, up since 2026-09-23, predating the Heimdall embed-watchdog fix committed 2026-09-26 -- Node does not hot-reload, so that fix had never actually run in the live process) -- confirmed cleanly shut down and relaunched with the same topology, Heimdall's own re-forging visibly active on the fresh process (fold-8812/fold-8819 detected down and re-forged automatically in the fresh log). The user explicitly redirected away from further chasing the Ollama embed issue specifically ("i keep saying, i dont know if ollama can handle embedding and even if so we dont need it") and noted embedding, if ever needed, could be done locally or in-browser instead -- recorded here for continuity, not acted on further this cycle.

No archon dispute: arrange.js and the EOT parser are named by no archon in README.md's Handle table or archon-holocracy/archons.json, checked before this research (no code was edited this cycle, so no reason.mjs-gated write was needed beyond this ledger revision itself).

REVISION, 2026-09-26: closed the real, disclosed gap from last cycle -- native/the-fold/arrange.js's notesOf silently produced zero notes for every copular/predicate-adjective sentence ("X is not Y"), since it required both a subject and an object/oblique arc off the sentence root, which a predicate adjective structurally cannot have. First attempt gated the new branch on finding a literal `cop` arc; verified live against the exact real sentence that motivated this ('Freedom of speech under the First Amendment is not absolute.') and found this parser drops the copula node entirely for predicate adjectives -- the cop-only gate still produced zero claims. Corrected to gate on `root.upos === "ADJ"` (or a real cop arc when one is present) -- deliberately NOT "any non-verb root", because this session's own prior falsification found a genuine parser root-selection error also lands on a non-verb root (a bare NOUN, the science-domain 'energy' mis-root) -- admitting that case would have manufactured a false claim from an already-diagnosed parser error. Verified live on both real sentences: the legal thesis now correctly produces a real, negated copular claim (freedom -be(-)-> absolute) and reads loadBearing:true; the science thesis, still wrongly rooted on a noun, correctly still produces zero claims, unchanged.

Found a SEPARATE, more serious, pre-existing bug while verifying this against the existing test suite: loadBearingChecker (claim-dependencies.js) never seeded consequentialSurprise's own null-simulation rng, which defaults to Math.random -- mechanically reproduced by calling the SAME candidate, SAME claim universe, SAME pValue five times in a row and observing the load-bearing verdict flip true/false non-deterministically, including disagreeing with itself WITHIN one process run (outline.thesis vs outline.thesisCandidates, both routed through the identical closure, for the identical candidate id). This is not new -- it has been present since loadBearingChecker was built, silently landing far enough from any significance boundary in every previous fixture to go unnoticed until today's copular-extraction fix changed the claim universe enough to land one real candidate right at a noisy boundary. Fixed by passing `seeded(candidateId)` (english-parser.js's own already-established PRNG, the same convention pocket-discovery-gap.js already uses for its own null trials) into consequentialSurprise's rng option. Verified: the same five-times mechanical reproduction, re-run after the fix, now agrees 5/5, and the internal thesis-vs-thesisCandidates cross-check for the identical id also agrees. This means every prior loadBearing value this session recorded in the ledger as a "measured fact" was, in the strict sense, a single random draw rather than a reproducible measurement -- disclosed here honestly; none is retracted, since none is known to have been wrong, only unverified-as-reproducible until now.

Updated arrange-loadbearing.test.mjs to match the new, correct, now-stable real behavior (re-verified 3x): "was very lazy" (a copular sentence) now correctly reads loadBearing:false (a real claim exists, not load-bearing) instead of the old null ("nothing extractable"). Re-ran the full relevant suite after all fixes: 109/109 passing (arrange-loadbearing, arrange-falsify, claims-from-feat, fold-at, claim-dependencies, cli/fold-at, loop-check-falsify, referent-verify-falsify, admission-falsify), no regressions.

Still open, honestly: the science-domain parser root-selection error remains a real, disclosed, unfixed gap (matches an already-measured parser accuracy ceiling); whether other real sentence shapes beyond SVO and predicate-adjective exist that notesOf still silently skips is unknown and not swept for this cycle.

REVISION THIS CYCLE: a real, mechanically falsifiable experiment on the "holon is both a whole and a part" question raised in conversation -- does treating a body-group's claims as one pooled WHOLE (a single consequentialSurprise check over the union) agree with the existing bottom-up PARTS-aggregate (any-member-true, already built into arrange.js's bodySlots)? Added claim-dependencies.js's loadBearingOfWhole, purely additive (loadBearingChecker itself untouched, zero deleted lines). Ran it across every real content fixture used this session (Cumberland River history, a legal excerpt, a photosynthesis excerpt, a bicycle-brake excerpt) at pValue=0.05: 15 of 16 real body-groups agree, and exactly one real, reproducible disagreement was found -- the Cumberland fixture's own body-6 (the Army Corps dam-building paragraph, p6.1/p6.2/p6.3) reads parts=true but whole=false. Locked into a committed, deterministic test (holonic-tension.test.mjs, re-verified stable across 3 runs); full relevant suite re-run at 60/60 passing (including the peer session's own contacts tests, confirmed compatible).

A sentence passing this stale filter shipped directly as `buf` -- the real, complete isMetaSentence in this same function only ran later, on entirely different candidates, in a fallback branch reached only when the stale filter admitted nothing at all.

Confirmed live, mechanically, before and after: the real isMetaSentence correctly catches the leak, chat-voice phrasing, and the original task-talk pattern; the stale inline regex would only have caught the last of those three. Fixed by replacing the inline regex with a direct call to the same isMetaSentence function the sibling admission loop 20 lines above already uses correctly -- removing the drift risk itself rather than patching the regex a third time. Grepped the rest of the codebase for any other hand-copied instance of the same pattern: none found: this was the only other copy.

title: How this vision gets chased (revised: Houdini turned on numbers -- fixed the clearest hand-set-threshold violation found, built a real reusable candidate-finder, named the rest honestly rather than inventing fixes)
text:
Per direct instruction to debunk every hand-set number, per this project's own oldest standing rule ("no hand-set thresholds -- measure a null instead"). Searched real files (proxy-runner.mjs, heimdall.mjs, archon-rules.js, admission.js, referent-verify.js, prosify.js, finish.js, ablation-grain-pressure.js, fold-at.js, claim-dependencies.js, pipeline-run.mjs, pacing.js) and verified the strongest candidates by hand before acting.

Fixed the clearest, real violation: proxy-runner.mjs's convo-window decay computed gamma via a ternary that silently substituted an invented 0.8 whenever the configured window was invalid -- directly bypassing kernel/activation.js's own gammaFor(), which explicitly REFUSES to default ("window is declared... never a default", it throws). Fixed at the boundary: WINDOW is now clamped to gammaFor's own documented minimum (2) or the file's own pre-existing default (12) -- never a third, new number -- so gammaFor is always called, never worked around. Verified the clamp handles zero, negative, and NaN env-var values correctly, and that gammaFor still throws for genuinely invalid direct calls.

Built a real, reusable tool rather than a one-off fix: cli/houdini-numbers.mjs, a candidate-finder for numeric literals sitting beside a comparison operator, minus a disclosed, narrow structural-exclusion list (array indices, .length checks against 0/1 specifically -- not against any other number, HTTP status codes, timeout/budget configs), cross-checked against a disclosed list of measured-justification markers this codebase's own comments already use. Explicitly disclosed in its own header and output as a heuristic candidate finder, never a classifier -- caught real, already-hand-verified specimens in testing (referent-verify.js's bare 20-character admission cutoff; finish.js's two 12-character candidate-length cutoffs) and 6 real tests lock this in against those exact specimens, not synthetic fixtures. Also confirmed its own real, disclosed limits: it cannot see arithmetic-blend formulas (proxy-runner.mjs's Kelsen gauge, 0.3 + ratio*0.6) or comparisons against named-but-defaulted parameters (resolutionFor's coarseAt/fineAt) -- a different pattern than a direct literal comparison, not attempted here.

Named, not fixed, the rest found this cycle: an inconsistency between two unmeasured "is this candidate substantial enough" cutoffs (20 characters in referent-verify.js/prosify.js vs 12 in finish.js, same kind of decision, no shared measurement behind either number) -- fixing this by picking a third number would repeat the exact mistake being debunked; it needs a real null test over real sentence-length distributions first. Also named: pacing.js's flatline/blink/dense-sentence ratios (0.65, 0.3, 8-word floor), a low-recall rewrite trigger at 0.5, and heimdall.mjs's own box-saturation cutoff (10% idle) -- the last of which the file's own comments already flag as monitored-but-unproven, which this session confirms rather than newly discovers.

No archon dispute: registry.mjs reported 0 live archons, 0 open disputes, checked before editing.
basis: Fixed the one violation that directly contradicted an existing, deliberate refuse-to-default guard elsewhere in the same codebase; built a real, tested, disclosed-as-imperfect tool so this becomes a standing, re-runnable capability rather than a one-time manual find; named the remaining real candidates honestly rather than inventing compromise numbers to look complete.
